1.159.m: who is like Ananta among serpents, of whom all yogins are [portions], / possessing a thousand heads and red eyes, alongside unsurpassable [serpents] such as Śeṣa;

1.159.s:
yo yajña iti vipreṃdrairarcyate sukhamīpsubhiḥ ..
sarve ca yaṃ yataprāṇā dhyāyanti brahmarūpiṇam .. 19 ..
1.159.d:
यो यज्ञ इति विप्रेंद्रैरर्च्यते सुखमीप्सुभिः ॥
सर्वे च यं यतप्राणा ध्यायन्ति ब्रह्मरूपिणम् ॥ 19 ॥
1.159.m: who is worshipped as sacrifice by eminent Brahmins seeking happiness, / and upon whom, as having the form of Brahman, all those with controlled breath meditate;

1.159.s:
yaṃ vedavido gāyaṃti vettāraṃ yajñadāyi nam ..
taṃ putraṃ dvādaśātmānaṃ kaśyapaḥ prāpya sattamam .. 1.159.20 ..
1.159.d:
यं वेदविदो गायंति वेत्तारं यज्ञदायि नम् ॥
तं पुत्रं द्वादशात्मानं कश्यपः प्राप्य सत्तमम् ॥ 1.159.20 ॥
1.159.m: whom the knowers of the Vedas sing as the knower and the giver of sacrifice— / having obtained that best son possessing twelve forms,

1.159.s:
mudaṃ lebhe sahādityā sukhaṃ ca paramaṃ vibho ..
lokaśca mumude sarvo rākṣasā bhayamāpnu van .. 21 ..
1.159.d:
मुदं लेभे सहादित्या सुखं च परमं विभो ॥
लोकश्च मुमुदे सर्वो राक्षसा भयमाप्नु वन् ॥ 21 ॥
1.159.m: Kaśyapa, along with Aditi, experienced supreme delight and happiness, O mighty one; / and the entire world rejoiced, while the rākṣasas fell into fear.

1.159.s:
madhupiṃgalo mahābāhuḥ kaṃbugrīvo hasanniva ..
iṃgudībaddhamukuṭo diśaḥ prajvalayanniva .. 22 ..
1.159.d:
मधुपिंगलो महाबाहुः कंबुग्रीवो हसन्निव ॥
इंगुदीबद्धमुकुटो दिशः प्रज्वलयन्निव ॥ 22 ॥
1.159.m: He had honey-tawny eyes, mighty arms, a conch-like neck, and a smiling countenance, as it were; / wearing a diadem tied with ingudī, he seemed to set the directions ablaze.

1.159.s:
sa uvāca mahātejāḥ kaśyapaṃ carṣisatta mam ..
eṣohaṃ tava putratvaṃ gato garbhasya siddhaye .. 23 ..
1.159.d:
स उवाच महातेजाः कश्यपं चर्षिसत्त मम् ॥
एषोहं तव पुत्रत्वं गतो गर्भस्य सिद्धये ॥ 23 ॥
1.159.m: Of immense splendour, he spoke to Kaśyapa, the best of sages: / "Here I have become your son for the perfection of the womb.

1.159.s:
dattvā varaṃ purā vipra viraṃcasya mahātmanaḥ ..
tasmāttvamṛṣiśārdūla kuru sṛṣṭimanaupamām .. .. 24 ..
1.159.d:
दत्त्वा वरं पुरा विप्र विरंचस्य महात्मनः ॥
तस्मात्त्वमृषिशार्दूल कुरु सृष्टिमनौपमाम् ॥ ॥ 24 ॥
1.159.m: Having granted a boon long ago, O Brahmin, to the great-souled Virañci, / therefore, O tiger among sages, produce an incomparable creation."

1.159.s:
evamārādhya deveśaṃ brahmā sṛṣṭimavāptavān ..
ārādhya kaśyapaścāpi bhāskaraṃ sutamāptavān .. 25 ..
sūryāvatāravarṇanam
1.159.d:
एवमाराध्य देवेशं ब्रह्मा सृष्टिमवाप्तवान् ॥
आराध्य कश्यपश्चापि भास्करं सुतमाप्तवान् ॥ 25 ॥
सूर्यावतारवर्णनम्
1.159.m:
Having worshipped the Lord of gods in this way, Brahmā obtained the creation; / and having worshipped the sun, Kaśyapa too obtained a son.
Description of the Incarnation of Sūrya

1.160.s:
.. śatānīka uvāca .. ..
aho devasya caritaṃ bhāskarasya tvayoditam ..
brahmādayo'pi yaṃ nityaṃ pūjayaṃti vidhānataḥ .. 1 ..
1.160.d:
॥ शतानीक उवाच ॥ ॥
अहो देवस्य चरितं भास्करस्य त्वयोदितम् ॥
ब्रह्मादयोऽपि यं नित्यं पूजयंति विधानतः ॥ 1 ॥
1.160.m: Śatānīka said: / "Ah, wonderful is the conduct of the Sun-god related by you, / whom even Brahmā and the others constantly worship according to rule.

1.160.s:
brahmā viṣṇuḥ surā brahmaṃstamārādhya divākaram ..
dadṛśustasya kiṃbhūtaṃ rūpaṃ yattanmahādbhutam .. 2 ..
1.160.d:
ब्रह्मा विष्णुः सुरा ब्रह्मंस्तमाराध्य दिवाकरम् ॥
ददृशुस्तस्य किंभूतं रूपं यत्तन्महाद्भुतम् ॥ 2 ॥
1.160.m: Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and the gods, O Brahmin, having worshipped that Sun— / what kind of form of his did they behold that was so greatly wondrous?"

1.160.s:
.. sumaṃturuvāca .. ..
ārādhya devamīśānaṃ bhāskaraṃ sūtivācakam ..
kaviṣṇū kuruśārdūla jagmatustau himācalam ..3..
1.160.d:
॥ सुमंतुरुवाच ॥ ॥
आराध्य देवमीशानं भास्करं सूतिवाचकम् ॥
कविष्णू कुरुशार्दूल जग्मतुस्तौ हिमाचलम् ॥3॥
1.160.m: Sumantu said: / "Having worshipped the divine Īśāna, and the Sun who proclaimed his birth, / Brahmā and Viṣṇu, O tiger of the Kurus, went to the Himālaya mountains.

1.160.s:
gopateraṃtikaṃ vīra prahṛṣṭau vibhudarśane ..
kuṃdeṃdusaṃnibhaṃ draṣṭuṃ kaṃjajaścācyutaśca tau ..4..
1.160.d:
गोपतेरंतिकं वीर प्रहृष्टौ विभुदर्शने ॥
कुंदेंदुसंनिभं द्रष्टुं कंजजश्चाच्युतश्च तौ ॥4॥
1.160.m: Rejoicing to see the god, they approached the Lord of rays, O hero; / Brahmā and Acyuta went to behold him who resembled the jasmine and the moon.

1.160.s:
dadṛśaturmahātmānaṃ caṃdrārdhakṛtaśekharam ..
pūjayaṃtaṃ vivasvaṃtaṃ bhāskaraṃ vīravannṛpa .. 5 ..
1.160.d:
ददृशतुर्महात्मानं चंद्रार्धकृतशेखरम् ॥
पूजयंतं विवस्वंतं भास्करं वीरवन्नृप ॥ 5 ॥
1.160.m: They beheld the great-souled [god] whose crest was adorned with the crescent moon, / worshipping Vivasvat, the Sun, like a hero, O king.

1.160.s:
ārcyocaturmahātmānaṃ kaviṣṇū taṃ trilocanam ..
bhobho bhīma suraśreṣṭha paśyāvāmiha cāgatau .. 6 ..
1.160.d:
आर्च्योचतुर्महात्मानं कविष्णू तं त्रिलोचनम् ॥
भोभो भीम सुरश्रेष्ठ पश्यावामिह चागतौ ॥ 6 ॥
1.160.m: Having paid homage to that great-souled three-eyed one, Brahmā and Viṣṇu said: / 'Hail, Bhīma, best of the gods! Look, both of us have arrived here!'

1.160.s:
śrutvovāca tayorvākyaṃ kaṃjajasyācyutasya ca ..
praṇamya śirasā bhūmau kṛtvā pūjāṃ vidhānataḥ ..7..
1.160.d:
श्रुत्वोवाच तयोर्वाक्यं कंजजस्याच्युतस्य च ॥
प्रणम्य शिरसा भूमौ कृत्वा पूजां विधानतः ॥7॥
1.160.m: Hearing the words of the two, the lotus-born [Brahmā] and Acyuta, / and having bowed his head to the ground and performed worship according to rule,

1.160.s:
uvāca madhuraṃ vākyaṃ śikṣākṣarasamanvitam ..
harṣa gadgadayā vācā diśaḥ sannādayanniva .. 8 ..
1.160.d:
उवाच मधुरं वाक्यं शिक्षाक्षरसमन्वितम् ॥
हर्ष गद्गदया वाचा दिशः सन्नादयन्निव ॥ 8 ॥
1.160.m: he spoke sweet words endowed with instructive syllables, / with a voice faltering through joy, making the directions resound as it were:

1.160.s:
kimārādhya raviṃ prāptau sarvadevavaraṃ vibhum ..
kathyatāṃ nikhilaṃ devau paramaṃ kautukaṃ mama .. 9 ..
1.160.d:
किमाराध्य रविं प्राप्तौ सर्वदेववरं विभुम् ॥
कथ्यतां निखिलं देवौ परमं कौतुकं मम ॥ 9 ॥
1.160.m: 'Having worshipped Ravi, the all-pervading foremost of all gods, what have you attained? / Let it all be told, O two gods; great is my curiosity!

1.160.s:
dṛṣṭavaṃtau paraṃ kiṃcidrūpaṃ devasya śaṃkaram ..
avyayasyāprameyasya bhānoramitatejasaḥ ..1.160.1 0..
1.160.d:
दृष्टवंतौ परं किंचिद्रूपं देवस्य शंकरम् ॥
अव्ययस्याप्रमेयस्य भानोरमिततेजसः ॥1.160.1 0॥
1.160.m: Did you behold any supreme, auspicious form of that god, / of the imperishable, immeasurable Sun of boundless radiance?'

1.160.s:
niśamya vacanaṃ vīra śaṃkarasya mahātmanaḥ ..
ūcatustau mahātmānau kaviṣṇū devasattamau ..11..
1.160.d:
निशम्य वचनं वीर शंकरस्य महात्मनः ॥
ऊचतुस्तौ महात्मानौ कविष्णू देवसत्तमौ ॥11॥
1.160.m: Hearing the words of the great-souled Śaṅkara, O hero, / those two great-souled, best of gods, Brahmā and Viṣṇu, said:

1.160.s:
na tatpaśyāvahe rūpaṃ yattatparamamadbhutam ..
ārādhayitumevāpi hyāgatau teṃtikaṃ ca tam ..12..
1.160.d:
न तत्पश्यावहे रूपं यत्तत्परममद्भुतम् ॥
आराधयितुमेवापि ह्यागतौ तेंतिकं च तम् ॥12॥
1.160.m: 'We have not seen that form which is supreme and wondrous; / indeed, we have come to your presence so that we may worship him.

1.160.s:
tasmādārādhayāmo hi ekībhūya vibhāvasum..
gatvodayagiriṃ puṇyaṃ parvataṃ kanakojjvalam..13..
1.160.d:
तस्मादाराधयामो हि एकीभूय विभावसुम्॥
गत्वोदयगिरिं पुण्यं पर्वतं कनकोज्ज्वलम्॥13॥
1.160.m: Therefore, uniting together, let us worship the Sun, / having gone to the sacred Udayagiri, the mountain shining like gold.'

1.160.s:
śrutvā tu vacanaṃ vīra kaṃjajācyutayorharaḥ..
tathetyāha mahābāho harṣādutphullalocanaḥ.. ..14..
1.160.d:
श्रुत्वा तु वचनं वीर कंजजाच्युतयोर्हरः॥
तथेत्याह महाबाहो हर्षादुत्फुल्ललोचनः॥ ॥14॥
1.160.m: Hearing the words of the lotus-born [Brahmā] and Acyuta, O hero, Hara, / his eyes blossoming with joy, said, 'So be it,' O mighty-armed one.

1.160.s:
atha te rājaśārdūla vivigogatayo nṛpa ..
jagmustaṃ parvataśreṣṭhamudayācalamāśu vai ..15..
1.160.d:
अथ ते राजशार्दूल विविगोगतयो नृप ॥
जग्मुस्तं पर्वतश्रेष्ठमुदयाचलमाशु वै ॥15॥
1.160.m: Then, O tiger among kings, moving unimpeded through the sky, O king, / they quickly went to that best of mountains, the Udayācala.

1.160.s:
tamāsādya nagaṃ puṇyaṃ śṛṃgaistribhiralaṃkṛtam ..
nānā dhātupinaddhāṅgaṃ nānādhātuvibhūṣitam .. 16 ..
1.160.d:
तमासाद्य नगं पुण्यं शृंगैस्त्रिभिरलंकृतम् ॥
नाना धातुपिनद्धाङ्गं नानाधातुविभूषितम् ॥ 16 ॥
1.160.m: Reaching that holy mountain adorned with three peaks, / its body covered with various minerals and embellished with various ores,

1.160.s:
ārādhanāya vidhivadyatnaṃ cakrurvibhāvasoḥ ..
stuvantaste samarcaṃto dhyāyaṃtaśca vibhāvasum .. 17 ..
1.160.d:
आराधनाय विधिवद्यत्नं चक्रुर्विभावसोः ॥
स्तुवन्तस्ते समर्चंतो ध्यायंतश्च विभावसुम् ॥ 17 ॥
1.160.m: they made an effort to worship the Sun according to rule, / praising, properly venerating, and meditating upon the Sun.

1.160.s:
divyavarṣasahasrāṃte tapaṃtaḥ saṃsthitā nage ..
padmāsanagato brahmā dhyāyamāno divākaram ..18..
1.160.d:
दिव्यवर्षसहस्रांते तपंतः संस्थिता नगे ॥
पद्मासनगतो ब्रह्मा ध्यायमानो दिवाकरम् ॥18॥
1.160.m: At the end of a thousand divine years, performing austerities, they remained on the mountain: / Brahmā was seated in the lotus posture, meditating on the Sun;

1.160.s:
sthāṇuvatsaṃsthito bhūmāvūrdhvabāhustrilocanaḥ ..
paṃcāgniṃ bhajamānastu sthito viṣṇuravākchirāḥ .. 19 ..
1.160.d:
स्थाणुवत्संस्थितो भूमावूर्ध्वबाहुस्त्रिलोचनः ॥
पंचाग्निं भजमानस्तु स्थितो विष्णुरवाक्छिराः ॥ 19 ॥
1.160.m: the three-eyed one stood on the ground like a pillar, with his arms raised up; / and Viṣṇu stood head downwards, devoted to the five fires.

1.160.s:
evaṃ varṣasahasrāṃte tapaścakruḥ sudāruṇam ..
ārādhayaṃto vidhivadgopatiṃ putramālinam .. 1.160.20 ..
1.160.d:
एवं वर्षसहस्रांते तपश्चक्रुः सुदारुणम् ॥
आराधयंतो विधिवद्गोपतिं पुत्रमालिनम् ॥ 1.160.20 ॥
1.160.m: Thus, at the end of a thousand years, they performed extremely severe austerity, / worshipping according to rule the Lord of rays, who is garlanded with rays.

1.160.s:
atha brahmeśaviṣṇūnāṃ kurvatāṃ tapa uttamam ..
tutoṣa bhagavānbhānuruvāca ca mahīpate .. 21 ..
1.160.d:
अथ ब्रह्मेशविष्णूनां कुर्वतां तप उत्तमम् ॥
तुतोष भगवान्भानुरुवाच च महीपते ॥ 21 ॥
1.160.m: Then, as Brahmā, Īśa, and Viṣṇu were performing excellent austerity, / the blessed Sun was pleased and spoke, O lord of the earth:

1.160.s:
brahmañchaṃbho hare brūta mattaḥ kimabhivāṃchatha ..
tuṣṭohaṃ bhavatāṃ dātu mihāyāto varaṃ svayam .. 22 ..
1.160.d:
ब्रह्मञ्छंभो हरे ब्रूत मत्तः किमभिवांछथ ॥
तुष्टोहं भवतां दातु मिहायातो वरं स्वयम् ॥ 22 ॥
1.160.m: "O Brahmā, Śambhu, and Hari! Speak! What do you desire from me? / Pleased with you, I have come here in person to grant a boon."

1.160.s:
.. sumaṃturuvāca .. ..
niśamya vacanaṃ bhānoḥ śāṃtaṃ hṛdyaṃ manoramam ..
praṇamya śirasā keśā idaṃ vacamabruvan.. .. 23 ..
1.160.d:
॥ सुमंतुरुवाच ॥ ॥
निशम्य वचनं भानोः शांतं हृद्यं मनोरमम् ॥
प्रणम्य शिरसा केशा इदं वचमब्रुवन्॥ ॥ 23 ॥
1.160.m: Sumantu said: / "Hearing the peaceful, cordial, and delightful speech of the Sun, / the gods bowed their heads and spoke these words:

1.160.s:
kṛtakṛtyā vayaṃ sarve prasādāttava gopate ..
tvāmārādhya purā deva tvattaḥ prāpya varaṃ śubham .. 24 ..
1.160.d:
कृतकृत्या वयं सर्वे प्रसादात्तव गोपते ॥
त्वामाराध्य पुरा देव त्वत्तः प्राप्य वरं शुभम् ॥ 24 ॥
1.160.m: 'All of us have accomplished our aims through your grace, O Lord of rays, / having worshipped you formerly, O god, and obtained an auspicious boon from you.

1.160.s:
utpattisthitināśānāṃ vayaṃ sarve divākara ..
saṃbhūyeha samarthā vai tvatprasādānna saṃśayaḥ .. 25 ..
1.160.d:
उत्पत्तिस्थितिनाशानां वयं सर्वे दिवाकर ॥
संभूयेह समर्था वै त्वत्प्रसादान्न संशयः ॥ 25 ॥
1.160.m: All of us together, O Sun, have become capable / of origination, maintenance, and destruction here through your grace; of this there is no doubt.

1.160.s:
kiṃ tvekaṃ devadeveśa varamicchāmahe vibho ..
yatte paramakaṃ rūpaṃ durlabhaṃ durdṛśaṃ tathā .. 26 ..
1.160.d:
किं त्वेकं देवदेवेश वरमिच्छामहे विभो ॥
यत्ते परमकं रूपं दुर्लभं दुर्दृशं तथा ॥ 26 ॥
1.160.m: Yet we desire one boon, O God of the lords of the gods, O all-pervading one: / that which is your supreme form, hard to attain and difficult to behold—

1.160.s:
tasmādasmājjagannātha rūpaṃ darśaya te'cyutam ..
sarvadevamayaṃ yatte yattvayoktaṃ purānagha ..27..
1.160.d:
तस्मादस्माज्जगन्नाथ रूपं दर्शय तेऽच्युतम् ॥
सर्वदेवमयं यत्ते यत्त्वयोक्तं पुरानघ ॥27॥
1.160.m: therefore, show us, O Lord of the universe, your imperishable form, / which comprises all the gods, as spoken of by you formerly, O sinless one!'

1.160.s:
teṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā brahmaviṣṇvīśabhāṣitam..
darśayāmāsa tadrūpamadbhutaṃ lokapūjitam .. 28 ..
1.160.d:
तेषां तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा ब्रह्मविष्ण्वीशभाषितम्॥
दर्शयामास तद्रूपमद्भुतं लोकपूजितम् ॥ 28 ॥
1.160.m: Hearing those words of theirs, spoken by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Īśa, / he revealed that wondrous form revered by the world,

1.160.s:
anekavaktraśirasamanekādbhutadarśanam ..
sarvadevamayaṃ divyaṃ sarvalokamayaṃ tathā .. 29 ..
1.160.d:
अनेकवक्त्रशिरसमनेकाद्भुतदर्शनम् ॥
सर्वदेवमयं दिव्यं सर्वलोकमयं तथा ॥ 29 ॥
1.160.m: having manifold faces and heads, of manifold wonderful sights, / divine, embodying all the gods, and embodying all the worlds.

1.160.s:
bhūḥ pādau dyauḥ śiraścāpi tatrāgnī locane mate ..
pādāṃgulyaḥ piśācāśca hastāṃgulyaśca guhyakāḥ .. 1.160.30 ..
1.160.d:
भूः पादौ द्यौः शिरश्चापि तत्राग्नी लोचने मते ॥
पादांगुल्यः पिशाचाश्च हस्तांगुल्यश्च गुह्यकाः ॥ 1.160.30 ॥
1.160.m: The earth was his feet, heaven his head, and both fires were held to be his eyes; / his toes were the piśācas, and his fingers were the guhyakas.

1.160.s:
viśve devāḥ smṛtāstasya jaṃghāsaṃghāḥ surottamāḥ ..
yakṣāḥ kukṣiṣu saṃlīnāḥ keśāścāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ ..31..
1.160.d:
विश्वे देवाः स्मृतास्तस्य जंघासंघाः सुरोत्तमाः ॥
यक्षाः कुक्षिषु संलीनाः केशाश्चाप्सरसां गणाः ॥31॥
1.160.m: The All-gods, best of deities, were regarded as the mass of his shanks; / the yakṣas rested within his sides, and the hosts of apsarases were his hair.

1.160.s:
dṛṣṭidhṛṣṭyaśca vipulāḥ keśā vīrāṃśavaḥ smṛtāḥ ..
tārakā romarūpāṇi romāṇi ca maharṣayaḥ ..32..
1.160.d:
दृष्टिधृष्ट्यश्च विपुलाः केशा वीरांशवः स्मृताः ॥
तारका रोमरूपाणि रोमाणि च महर्षयः ॥32॥
1.160.m: His vast gazes and bold glances, and his locks of hair, were regarded as his heroic rays; / the stars were his body-hairs, and the great sages were his body-hair.

1.160.s:
bāhavo vidiśastasya diśaḥ śrotre narādhipa..
aśvinau śravaṇe cāsya nāsā vāyurmahābalaḥ ..33..
1.160.d:
बाहवो विदिशस्तस्य दिशः श्रोत्रे नराधिप॥
अश्विनौ श्रवणे चास्य नासा वायुर्महाबलः ॥33॥
1.160.m: The intermediate quarters were his arms, the cardinal directions his ears, O ruler of men; / the two Aśvins were his hearing, and his nose was the mighty Wind.

1.160.s:
prasādaśca kṣamā caiva mano dharmastathaiva ca ..
satyamasyābhavadvāṇī jihvā devī sarasvatī .. 34 ..
1.160.d:
प्रसादश्च क्षमा चैव मनो धर्मस्तथैव च ॥
सत्यमस्याभवद्वाणी जिह्वा देवी सरस्वती ॥ 34 ॥
1.160.m: Benevolence and forbearance were his mind, and dharma likewise; / truth was his speech, and the goddess Sarasvatī was his tongue.

1.160.s:
grīvāditirmahādevī tālū rudraśca vīryavān ..
dvāraṃ svargasya nābhirvai mitrastvaṣṭā picaṃḍakaḥ .. 35 ..
1.160.d:
ग्रीवादितिर्महादेवी तालू रुद्रश्च वीर्यवान् ॥
द्वारं स्वर्गस्य नाभिर्वै मित्रस्त्वष्टा पिचंडकः ॥ 35 ॥
1.160.m: His neck is the great goddess Aditi, and his palate is the powerful Rudra; / the gateway of heaven is indeed his navel, and Mitra and Tvaṣṭṛ are his belly.

1.160.s:
mukhaṃ vaiśvānaraścāsya vṛṣaṇau ca bhagastadā ..
hṛdayaṃ bhagavānbrahmā hyudaraṃ kaśyapo muniḥ .. 36 ..
1.160.d:
मुखं वैश्वानरश्चास्य वृषणौ च भगस्तदा ॥
हृदयं भगवान्ब्रह्मा ह्युदरं कश्यपो मुनिः ॥ 36 ॥
1.160.m: Vaiśvānara is his mouth, and then Bhaga is his testicles; / Lord Brahmā is his heart, and the sage Kaśyapa is his abdomen.

1.160.s:
pṛṣṭhe'sya vasavo devā marutaḥ sarvasaṃdhiṣu ..
sarvacchaṃdāṃsi daśanā jyotīṃṣi vimalā prabhā .. 37 ..
1.160.d:
पृष्ठेऽस्य वसवो देवा मरुतः सर्वसंधिषु ॥
सर्वच्छंदांसि दशना ज्योतींषि विमला प्रभा ॥ 37 ॥
1.160.m: On his back are the Vasu gods, and the Maruts in all his joints; / all the metres are his teeth, and the heavenly luminaries are his spotless radiance.

1.160.s:
prāṇo rudro mahādevaḥ kukṣau cāsya mahārṇavāḥ ..
udare cāsya gaṃdharvā bhujagāśca mahābalāḥ .. 38 ..
1.160.d:
प्राणो रुद्रो महादेवः कुक्षौ चास्य महार्णवाः ॥
उदरे चास्य गंधर्वा भुजगाश्च महाबलाः ॥ 38 ॥
1.160.m: His breath is Rudra, the great god, and in his side are the great oceans; / in his belly are the Gandharvas and the mighty serpents.

1.160.s:
lakṣmīrmedhā dhṛtiḥ kāṃtiḥ sarvā vidyāśca vai kaṭau ..
lalāṭamasya paramaṃ vayaḥsthānaṃ parātmanaḥ .. 39 ..
1.160.d:
लक्ष्मीर्मेधा धृतिः कांतिः सर्वा विद्याश्च वै कटौ ॥
ललाटमस्य परमं वयःस्थानं परात्मनः ॥ 39 ॥
1.160.m: Lakṣmī, intelligence, fortitude, beauty, and all the sciences are in his hips; / his forehead is the supreme abode of the prime of life for the supreme soul.

1.160.s:
sarvajyotīṃṣi jānīhi tapaścakraśca deva rāṭ..
tadetadādidevasya tanau hyāhurmahātmanaḥ .. 1.160.40 ..
1.160.d:
सर्वज्योतींषि जानीहि तपश्चक्रश्च देव राट्॥
तदेतदादिदेवस्य तनौ ह्याहुर्महात्मनः ॥ 1.160.40 ॥
1.160.m: Know all luminaries, austerity, the discus, and Indra [to be him]; / this is what they call present in the body of that primeval deity, the great soul.

1.160.s:
stanau kukṣau ca vedāśca teṣṭau cāsya makhāḥ smṛtāḥ ..
yaṣṭavyapaśubaṃdhāśca dvijānāṃ veṣṭi tāni ca .. 41 ..
1.160.d:
स्तनौ कुक्षौ च वेदाश्च तेष्टौ चास्य मखाः स्मृताः ॥
यष्टव्यपशुबंधाश्च द्विजानां वेष्टि तानि च ॥ 41 ॥
1.160.m: His breasts and sides are the Vedas, and these are known as his eight sacrifices; / they are also the animal offerings to be performed, and he envelops those of the twice-born.

1.160.s:
sarvadevamayaṃ dṛṣṭvā rūpamarkasya te nṛpa ..
brahmā haro harirdevāḥ paraṃ vismayamāgatāḥ .. 42 ..
1.160.d:
सर्वदेवमयं दृष्ट्वा रूपमर्कस्य ते नृप ॥
ब्रह्मा हरो हरिर्देवाः परं विस्मयमागताः ॥ 42 ॥
1.160.m: Beholding that form of the Sun, composed of all gods, O king, / Brahmā, Hara, Hari, and the gods were struck with supreme wonder.

1.160.s:
praṇamya śirasā devaṃ vepamānā dharāṃ gatāḥ ..
bhayagadgadayā vācā idaṃ vacanamabruvan.. 43 ..
1.160.d:
प्रणम्य शिरसा देवं वेपमाना धरां गताः ॥
भयगद्गदया वाचा इदं वचनमब्रुवन्॥ 43 ॥
1.160.m: Bowing to the god with their heads, trembling, they fell to the ground; / and with voices stammering from fear, they spoke these words:

1.160.s:
samīkṣya rūpaṃ te deva bhīmaṃ jvālāsamākulam ..
anekamukhabāhūrucaraṇaṃ cakitā vayam..44..
1.160.d:
समीक्ष्य रूपं ते देव भीमं ज्वालासमाकुलम् ॥
अनेकमुखबाहूरुचरणं चकिता वयम्॥44॥
1.160.m: “Beholding your terrible form filled with flames, O Lord, / with many faces, arms, thighs, and feet, we are terrified.

1.160.s:
digjñānaṃ hṛtamasmākaṃ tatprasīda jagatpate ..
upasaṃhara viśvātmandraṣṭuṃ śaktā na te vayam .. 45 ..
1.160.d:
दिग्ज्ञानं हृतमस्माकं तत्प्रसीद जगत्पते ॥
उपसंहर विश्वात्मन्द्रष्टुं शक्ता न ते वयम् ॥ 45 ॥
1.160.m: Our sense of direction is stolen away; therefore be gracious, O Lord of the universe! / Withdraw it, O soul of all! We are unable to look upon you.”

1.160.s:
iti teṣāṃ vacaḥ śrutvā devadevo divākaraḥ ..
prasanno bhagavānāha vacastānprahasannidam .. 46 ..
1.160.d:
इति तेषां वचः श्रुत्वा देवदेवो दिवाकरः ॥
प्रसन्नो भगवानाह वचस्तान्प्रहसन्निदम् ॥ 46 ॥
1.160.m: Hearing their words, the god of gods, the maker of the day, / the blessed Lord, pleased, laughed gently and spoke these words to them:

1.160.s:
.. āditya uvāca .. ..
yadetatparamaṃ puṇyamadbhutaṃ lokabhāvanam..
dṛṣṭaṃ bhavadbhirdeveṃdrā mama sarvajaganmayam .. 47 ..
1.160.d:
॥ आदित्य उवाच ॥ ॥
यदेतत्परमं पुण्यमद्भुतं लोकभावनम्॥
दृष्टं भवद्भिर्देवेंद्रा मम सर्वजगन्मयम् ॥ 47 ॥
1.160.m: The Sun said: / “This supreme, meritorious, wondrous, world-sustaining [form], / composed of the entire universe, which has been seen by you, O lords of the gods,

1.160.s:
etanmayā prasannena yuṣmākaṃ śreyase'naghāḥ ..
darśitaṃ pūjiteneha yogināṃ yanmahālayam .. 48 ..
1.160.d:
एतन्मया प्रसन्नेन युष्माकं श्रेयसेऽनघाः ॥
दर्शितं पूजितेनेह योगिनां यन्महालयम् ॥ 48 ॥
1.160.m: has been revealed by me, well-pleased, for your welfare, O sinless ones, / [now that I am] worshipped here—that which is the great abode of yogins.”

1.160.s:
.. brahmeśācyutā ucuḥ .. ..
evametanna saṃdeho yathāttha tvaṃ divaspate ..
yogināmapi deveśa darśanaṃ hyasya durlabham .. 49 ..
1.160.d:
॥ ब्रह्मेशाच्युता उचुः ॥ ॥
एवमेतन्न संदेहो यथात्थ त्वं दिवस्पते ॥
योगिनामपि देवेश दर्शनं ह्यस्य दुर्लभम् ॥ 49 ॥
1.160.m: Brahmā, Īśa, and Acyuta said: / “So it is; there is no doubt, just as you say, O Lord of heaven; / for the sight of this is hard to obtain even for yogins, O Lord of the gods.

1.160.s:
tvāmārādhya jagannāthaṃ nāprāpyamiha vidyate ..
tasmātpūjyatamo loke nānyo deveṣu vidyate .. 1.160.50 ..
1.160.d:
त्वामाराध्य जगन्नाथं नाप्राप्यमिह विद्यते ॥
तस्मात्पूज्यतमो लोके नान्यो देवेषु विद्यते ॥ 1.160.50 ॥
1.160.m: Having worshipped you, the Lord of the universe, there is nothing unattainable here; / therefore, no other among the gods is considered more worthy of worship in the world.”

1.160.s:
evamuktvā'diteḥ putro jagāmādarśanaṃ raviḥ ..
brahmādayopi te harṣaṃ prāpurdevasya darśanāt .. 51 ..
1.160.d:
एवमुक्त्वाऽदितेः पुत्रो जगामादर्शनं रविः ॥
ब्रह्मादयोपि ते हर्षं प्रापुर्देवस्य दर्शनात् ॥ 51 ॥
1.160.m: Having spoken thus, the Sun, son of Aditi, disappeared; / and Brahmā and the others attained joy from the vision of the god.

1.160.s:
evaṃ brahmādayo devāḥ pūjayitvā divākaram ..
gatāste paramāṃ siddhiṃ gaṃdharvā ṛṣayastathā .. 52 .. ..
sūryapūjāphalapraśnavarṇanam
1.160.d:
एवं ब्रह्मादयो देवाः पूजयित्वा दिवाकरम् ॥
गतास्ते परमां सिद्धिं गंधर्वा ऋषयस्तथा ॥ 52 ॥ ॥
सूर्यपूजाफलप्रश्नवर्णनम्
1.160.m:
Having worshipped the maker of the day in this manner, Brahmā and the other gods, / as well as the Gandharvas and sages, attained supreme perfection.
Description of the Question on the Fruit of Worshipping the Sun

1.161.s:
.. śatānīka uvāca .. ..
evametadyathāttha tvaṃ bhāskaro daivataṃ param ..
nāstyādityasamo devo nāstyādityasamā gatiḥ .. 1 ..
1.161.d:
॥ शतानीक उवाच ॥ ॥
एवमेतद्यथात्थ त्वं भास्करो दैवतं परम् ॥
नास्त्यादित्यसमो देवो नास्त्यादित्यसमा गतिः ॥ 1 ॥
1.161.m: Śatānīka said: / “So it is, just as you say: the Sun is the supreme deity; / there is no god equal to the Sun, no goal equal to the Sun.

1.161.s:
ādityamūlamakhilaṃ trailokyaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ ..
bhavatyasmājjagatsarvaṃ sadevāsuramānuṣam .. 2 ..
1.161.d:
आदित्यमूलमखिलं त्रैलोक्यं नात्र संशयः ॥
भवत्यस्माज्जगत्सर्वं सदेवासुरमानुषम् ॥ 2 ॥
1.161.m: The entire three worlds have the Sun as their root; of this there is no doubt; / the whole universe, together with gods, asuras, and humans, arises from him.

1.161.s:
rudreṃdropeṃdrakeṃdrāṇāṃ vipreṃdra tridivaukasām ..
dyutirdyutimatāṃ kṛtsnā tejo yatsārvalaukikam.. 3 ..
1.161.d:
रुद्रेंद्रोपेंद्रकेंद्राणां विप्रेंद्र त्रिदिवौकसाम् ॥
द्युतिर्द्युतिमतां कृत्स्ना तेजो यत्सार्वलौकिकम्॥ 3 ॥
1.161.m: Of Rudras, Indras, Upendras, and chiefs, O best of the twice-born, of the dwellers in heaven, / all the lustre of the lustrous, and whatever splendour belongs to all worlds—

1.161.s:
sarvātmā sarvalokeśo mahādevaḥ prajāpatiḥ ..
sūrya eva trilokasya mūlaṃ paramadaivatam .. 4 ..
1.161.d:
सर्वात्मा सर्वलोकेशो महादेवः प्रजापतिः ॥
सूर्य एव त्रिलोकस्य मूलं परमदैवतम् ॥ 4 ॥
1.161.m: he is the soul of all, the lord of all worlds, the great god, Prajāpati; / the Sun alone is the root of the three worlds, the supreme deity.

1.161.s:
tataḥ saṃjāyate sarvaṃ tatraiva pravilīyate ..
bhāvābhāvau hi lokanāmādityānniḥsṛtau purā .. 5 ..
1.161.d:
ततः संजायते सर्वं तत्रैव प्रविलीयते ॥
भावाभावौ हि लोकनामादित्यान्निःसृतौ पुरा ॥ 5 ॥
1.161.m: From him everything is born, and in him alone it dissolves; / for existence and non-existence of the worlds emerged from the Sun of old.

1.161.s:
jagajjyeṣṭho graho vipra pradīptaḥ prabhavo raviḥ ..
tatra gacchaṃti nidhanaṃ jāyaṃte ca punaḥ punaḥ .. 6 ..
1.161.d:
जगज्ज्येष्ठो ग्रहो विप्र प्रदीप्तः प्रभवो रविः ॥
तत्र गच्छंति निधनं जायंते च पुनः पुनः ॥ 6 ॥
1.161.m: He is the oldest planet in the world, O twice-born one, blazing, the source, the Sun; / into him they pass to destruction and are born again and again.

1.161.s:
kṣaṇā muhūrtā divasā rātripakṣāśca kṛtsnaśaḥ ..
māsāḥ saṃvatsarāścaiva ṛtavaśca yugāni ca .. 7 ..
1.161.d:
क्षणा मुहूर्ता दिवसा रात्रिपक्षाश्च कृत्स्नशः ॥
मासाः संवत्सराश्चैव ऋतवश्च युगानि च ॥ 7 ॥
1.161.m: The moments, muhūrtas, days, nights, and whole fortnights, / the months, years, seasons, and yugas—

1.161.s:
sa eṣa kālaścāgniśca dvādaśātmā prajāpatiḥ ..
prabhāsayati vipreṃdra trailokyaṃ sacarācaram .. 8 ..
1.161.d:
स एष कालश्चाग्निश्च द्वादशात्मा प्रजापतिः ॥
प्रभासयति विप्रेंद्र त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम् ॥ 8 ॥
1.161.m: he is Time and Fire, the twelve-fold Prajāpati; / he illuminates the three worlds with the moving and unmoving, O best of the twice-born.

1.161.s:
tasmādasya dvijaśreṣṭha pūjane yatphalaṃ bhavet ..
tanme brūhi prayatnena prasādapravaṇo bhava .. 9 .. ..
sauradharmavarṇanam
1.161.d:
तस्मादस्य द्विजश्रेष्ठ पूजने यत्फलं भवेत् ॥
तन्मे ब्रूहि प्रयत्नेन प्रसादप्रवणो भव ॥ 9 ॥ ॥
सौरधर्मवर्णनम्
1.161.m:
Therefore, O best of the twice-born, tell me diligently what fruit arises / from worshipping him; be inclined to grace!”
Description of Solar Duty

1.162.s:
.. sumaṃturuvāca .. ..
bhānuṃ pratiṣṭhāpya naraḥ sarvadevamayaṃ vibhum ..
prāpnotyamaratāṃ vīra tejasā ravisannibhaḥ .. 1 ..
1.162.d:
॥ सुमंतुरुवाच ॥ ॥
भानुं प्रतिष्ठाप्य नरः सर्वदेवमयं विभुम् ॥
प्राप्नोत्यमरतां वीर तेजसा रविसन्निभः ॥ 1 ॥
1.162.m: Sumantu said: / “A man who installs the Sun, the all-pervading lord who consists of all the gods, / attains immortality, O hero, resembling the Sun in splendour.

1.162.s:
yo bhānuṃ dveṣṭi saṃmohātsarvadevanama skṛtam ..
naro narakagāmī syāttasyasaṃbhāṣaṇādapi .. 2 ..
1.162.d:
यो भानुं द्वेष्टि संमोहात्सर्वदेवनम स्कृतम् ॥
नरो नरकगामी स्यात्तस्यसंभाषणादपि ॥ 2 ॥
1.162.m: The man who hates the Sun, who is bowed to by all gods, out of delusion, / goes to hell even merely from conversing with him.

1.162.s:
bhānumiṣṭaṃ pratiṣṭhāpya sarvayatnairvidhānataḥ ..
yatpuṇyaphalamāpnoti tadekāgramanāḥ śṛṇu .. .. 3 ..
1.162.d:
भानुमिष्टं प्रतिष्ठाप्य सर्वयत्नैर्विधानतः ॥
यत्पुण्यफलमाप्नोति तदेकाग्रमनाः शृणु ॥ ॥ 3 ॥
1.162.m: Having installed the beloved Sun according to rule with every effort, / hear with single-minded attention what meritorious fruit he obtains.

1.162.s:
sarvayajñatapodānatīrthadeveṣu yatphalam ..
tatphalaṃ koṭiguṇitaṃ sthāpya bhānuṃ labhennaraḥ .. 4 ..
1.162.d:
सर्वयज्ञतपोदानतीर्थदेवेषु यत्फलम् ॥
तत्फलं कोटिगुणितं स्थाप्य भानुं लभेन्नरः ॥ 4 ॥
1.162.m: Whatever fruit is obtained in all sacrifices, austerities, gifts, holy places, and gods, / multiplied ten-millionfold is the fruit a man obtains by installing the Sun.

1.162.s:
yo bhānuṃ sthāpayedbhaktyā vidhipūrvaṃ narādhipa ..
sarvāṃgamuditaṃ puṇyaṃ labhetkoṭiguṇaṃ naraḥ .. 5 ..
1.162.d:
यो भानुं स्थापयेद्भक्त्या विधिपूर्वं नराधिप ॥
सर्वांगमुदितं पुण्यं लभेत्कोटिगुणं नरः ॥ 5 ॥
1.162.m: A man who installs the Sun with devotion according to the prescribed rule, O king of men, / obtains all-limbed, elevated merit multiplied ten-millionfold.

1.162.s:
mātṛjānpitṛjāṃścaiva yatra codvahate striyam ..
kulatrayaṃ samuddhṛtya śakraloke mahīyate ..6..
1.162.d:
मातृजान्पितृजांश्चैव यत्र चोद्वहते स्त्रियम् ॥
कुलत्रयं समुद्धृत्य शक्रलोके महीयते ॥6॥
1.162.m: Delivering three lineages—the maternal, the paternal, and that from which he takes a wife— / he is glorified in the world of Indra.

1.162.s:
bhuktvā vipulānbhogānpralaye samupasthite ..
jñānayogaṃ samāsādya tatraiva pravimucyate .. 7 ..
1.162.d:
भुक्त्वा विपुलान्भोगान्प्रलये समुपस्थिते ॥
ज्ञानयोगं समासाद्य तत्रैव प्रविमुच्यते ॥ 7 ॥
1.162.m: Having enjoyed extensive pleasures, when the cosmic dissolution is at hand, / attaining the yoga of knowledge, he is liberated right there.

1.162.s:
atha vā rājyamākāṃkṣejjāyate saṃbhavāṃtare ..
saptadvīmasamudrāyāḥ kṣiteradhipatirbhavet .. 8 ..
1.162.d:
अथ वा राज्यमाकांक्षेज्जायते संभवांतरे ॥
सप्तद्वीमसमुद्रायाः क्षितेरधिपतिर्भवेत् ॥ 8 ॥
1.162.m: Or, if he should desire kingship, he is born in another life / as the sovereign ruler of the earth containing the seven continents and oceans.

1.162.s:
yatkṛtvā pārthivaṃ byomni arcayetsarvadevakam ..
samūlamakhilaṃ tena trailokyaṃ pūjitaṃ bhavet .. 9 ..
1.162.d:
यत्कृत्वा पार्थिवं ब्योम्नि अर्चयेत्सर्वदेवकम् ॥
समूलमखिलं तेन त्रैलोक्यं पूजितं भवेत् ॥ 9 ॥
1.162.m: Because by fashioning an earthen [image] of the Sun and worshipping all the gods [in it], / by him the entire three worlds are worshipped down to the very root.

1.162.s:
ihaiva dhanavāñcchrīmā nsoṃte'rkatvamavāpnuyāt ..
trisaṃdhyaṃ kīrtayedvyoma kṛtvā biṃbena pārthivam .. 1.162.10 ..
1.162.d:
इहैव धनवाञ्च्छ्रीमा न्सोंतेऽर्कत्वमवाप्नुयात् ॥
त्रिसंध्यं कीर्तयेद्व्योम कृत्वा बिंबेन पार्थिवम् ॥ 1.162.10 ॥
1.162.m: In this very life he becomes wealthy and prosperous, and in the end he attains union with the Sun; / at the three junctures of the day he should praise the Sun, having made an earthen [image] with its disk.

1.162.s:
śataikādaśakaṃ yāvattasya puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu ..
anena saha dehena bhānuḥ saṃtiṣṭhate kṣitau .. 11 ..
1.162.d:
शतैकादशकं यावत्तस्य पुण्यफलं शृणु ॥
अनेन सह देहेन भानुः संतिष्ठते क्षितौ ॥ 11 ॥
1.162.m: Hear the meritorious fruit of that for up to eleven hundred [years]: / with this very body, the Sun abides on the earth.

1.162.s:
pāpahā sarvamartyānāṃ darśanātsparśanādapi ..
uddhārayecca saṃsthāpya kulānāmekaviṃśatim .. 12 ..
1.162.d:
पापहा सर्वमर्त्यानां दर्शनात्स्पर्शनादपि ॥
उद्धारयेच्च संस्थाप्य कुलानामेकविंशतिम् ॥ 12 ॥
1.162.m: He destroys the sins of all mortals even through sight and touch; / and by installing it, he would deliver twenty-one generations.

1.162.s:
gīrvāṇaiḥ sahito nityaṃ modate divi sūravat ..
yo'pi piṣṭamayaṃ vyoma sarvagaṃdhopaśobhitam .. 13 ..
1.162.d:
गीर्वाणैः सहितो नित्यं मोदते दिवि सूरवत् ॥
योऽपि पिष्टमयं व्योम सर्वगंधोपशोभितम् ॥ 13 ॥
1.162.m: Together with the gods, he continuously rejoices in heaven like the Sun; / he also who [fashions an image of] the Sun made of flour, adorned with all perfumes—”

1.162.s:
kusumaiḥ susugaṃdhaiśca phalaiśca vividhairnṛpa ..
bhakṣyalehyarasaiścaiva kṛtadīpairalaṃkṛtaiḥ .. 14 ..
1.162.d:
कुसुमैः सुसुगंधैश्च फलैश्च विविधैर्नृप ॥
भक्ष्यलेह्यरसैश्चैव कृतदीपैरलंकृतैः ॥ 14 ॥
1.162.m: With flowers of sweet fragrance, and with various fruits, O king, / and with foods to be chewed, licked, and savoured, and with prepared lamps adorned,

1.162.s:
nānārasamāyuktaṃ nānāgaṃdhasamanvitam ..
tasya dakṣiṇapārśve tu vinyasedaguruṃ budhaḥ .. 15 ..
1.162.d:
नानारसमायुक्तं नानागंधसमन्वितम् ॥
तस्य दक्षिणपार्श्वे तु विन्यसेदगुरुं बुधः ॥ 15 ॥
1.162.m: endowed with various flavours and accompanied by diverse scents; / on its southern side, the wise man should place agallochum;

1.162.s:
dadyādvai paścime bhāge śrīkhaṃḍaṃ caṃdanaṃ śubham ..
uttare caṃdanaṃ dadyādraktaṃ dadyācca pūrvataḥ .. 16 ..
1.162.d:
दद्याद्वै पश्चिमे भागे श्रीखंडं चंदनं शुभम् ॥
उत्तरे चंदनं दद्याद्रक्तं दद्याच्च पूर्वतः ॥ 16 ॥
1.162.m: he should indeed offer auspicious white sandalwood on the western side; / he should offer sandalwood on the north, and red [sandalwood] on the east.

1.162.s:
evaṃ vittānusāreṇa kṛtvā vibhavavistaram ..
kṛṣṇapakṣe tu saptamyāṃ bhāska rasya nivedayet .. 17 ..
1.162.d:
एवं वित्तानुसारेण कृत्वा विभवविस्तरम् ॥
कृष्णपक्षे तु सप्तम्यां भास्क रस्य निवेदयेत् ॥ 17 ॥
1.162.m: Having thus made an expansive display of wealth according to his means, / he should present it to the Sun on the seventh lunar day of the dark fortnight.

1.162.s:
sakṛdeva tu yaḥ kuryādvyoma bharatasattama ..
yatphalaṃ hi bhavettasya tanme nigadataḥ śṛṇu .. 18 ..
1.162.d:
सकृदेव तु यः कुर्याद्व्योम भरतसत्तम ॥
यत्फलं हि भवेत्तस्य तन्मे निगदतः शृणु ॥ 18 ॥
1.162.m: Whoever should construct this celestial vault even once, O best of the Bharatas, / hear from me as I proclaim whatever fruit he gains:

1.162.s:
sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ sarvaduḥkhavivarjitaḥ ..
niṣkalaḥ sarvago bhūtvā praviśetparamavyayam ..
tejasā ravisaṃkāśaḥ prabhayārkasamaprabhaḥ .. 19 ..
1.162.d:
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तः सर्वदुःखविवर्जितः ॥
निष्कलः सर्वगो भूत्वा प्रविशेत्परमव्ययम् ॥
तेजसा रविसंकाशः प्रभयार्कसमप्रभः ॥ 19 ॥
1.162.m: Released from all sins, freed from all sorrow, / becoming partless and all-pervading, he would enter the supreme, imperishable [realm], / resembling the Sun in splendour, having radiance equal to the Sun.

1.162.s:
pāṃsunā krīḍamāno yaḥ kuryādvyoma hyakāryataḥ ..
sa rājanbhavate rājā parvateṣu samaṃtataḥ .. 1.162.20 ..
1.162.d:
पांसुना क्रीडमानो यः कुर्याद्व्योम ह्यकार्यतः ॥
स राजन्भवते राजा पर्वतेषु समंततः ॥ 1.162.20 ॥
1.162.m: Whoever, playing with dust, should construct a celestial vault, even playfully, / he becomes, O king, a king all around among the mountains.

1.162.s:
sarveṣāmeva pātrāṇāṃ paraṃ pātraṃ vibhāvasuḥ..
etatsaṃtārayedyasmādatīva narakārṇavāt .. 21 ..
1.162.d:
सर्वेषामेव पात्राणां परं पात्रं विभावसुः॥
एतत्संतारयेद्यस्मादतीव नरकार्णवात् ॥ 21 ॥
1.162.m: Among all recipients, the Sun is the supreme recipient, / since he carries [the devotee] safely across the vast ocean of hell.

1.162.s:
tasya pātrasya māhātmyaṃ dhruvamakṣayamādiśet ..
tasmāttasmai sadā deyamaprameyaphalārthibhiḥ .. 22 ..
1.162.d:
तस्य पात्रस्य माहात्म्यं ध्रुवमक्षयमादिशेत् ॥
तस्मात्तस्मै सदा देयमप्रमेयफलार्थिभिः ॥ 22 ॥
1.162.m: One should declare the greatness of that recipient to be constant and imperishable; / therefore, gifts should always be given to him by those desiring boundless fruit.

1.162.s:
ravau dattaṃ hutaṃ japtaṃ baliṃ pūjāṃ nivedayet ..
anaṃtaphalamādiṣṭaṃ brahmādisurasattamaiḥ .. 23 ..
1.162.d:
रवौ दत्तं हुतं जप्तं बलिं पूजां निवेदयेत् ॥
अनंतफलमादिष्टं ब्रह्मादिसुरसत्तमैः ॥ 23 ॥
1.162.m: Whatever is given, offered in fire, or chanted, or an offering or worship presented to the Sun, / has been declared to bear infinite fruit by the foremost gods, Brahmā and the others.

1.162.s:
bhaktyā vittānusāreṇa yaḥ kuryādālayaṃ raveḥ ..
sogneyaṃ yānamāruhya modate saha bhānunā .. 24 ..
1.162.d:
भक्त्या वित्तानुसारेण यः कुर्यादालयं रवेः ॥
सोग्नेयं यानमारुह्य मोदते सह भानुना ॥ 24 ॥
1.162.m: Whoever builds an abode for the Sun with devotion according to his means, / having mounted a fiery vehicle, rejoices together with the Sun.

1.162.s:
mahāvibhavasāropi yaḥ kuryādbhaktivarjitam..
alpe mahati vā tulyaṃ phalamāḍhyadaridrayoḥ .. 25 ..
1.162.d:
महाविभवसारोपि यः कुर्याद्भक्तिवर्जितम्॥
अल्पे महति वा तुल्यं फलमाढ्यदरिद्रयोः ॥ 25 ॥
1.162.m: Even if possessed of the essence of great wealth, whoever should build it destitute of devotion / — the fruit for the rich and the poor is equal, whether it be small or great.

1.162.s:
vittaśāṭhyena yaḥ kuryādvittavānapi mānavaḥ ..
na sa phalamavāpnoti pralobhākrāṃtamānasaḥ .. 26 ..
1.162.d:
वित्तशाठ्येन यः कुर्याद्वित्तवानपि मानवः ॥
न स फलमवाप्नोति प्रलोभाक्रांतमानसः ॥ 26 ॥
1.162.m: Even if possessing wealth, a man who acts with parsimony / does not attain the fruit, his mind being overcome with greed.

1.162.s:
tasmāttribhāgaṃ vittasya jīvanāya prakalpayet ..
bhāgadvayaṃ ca dharmārthe anityaṃ jīvanaṃ yataḥ .. 27 ..
1.162.d:
तस्मात्त्रिभागं वित्तस्य जीवनाय प्रकल्पयेत् ॥
भागद्वयं च धर्मार्थे अनित्यं जीवनं यतः ॥ 27 ॥
1.162.m: Therefore, one should assign one-third of one's wealth for livelihood, / and two parts for righteousness, because life is impermanent.

1.162.s:
bhaktyā pracoditaṃ kuryādalpavitto'pi yo naraḥ ..
mahāvibhavasāro'pi na kuryādbhaktivarjitaḥ .. 28 ..
1.162.d:
भक्त्या प्रचोदितं कुर्यादल्पवित्तोऽपि यो नरः ॥
महाविभवसारोऽपि न कुर्याद्भक्तिवर्जितः ॥ 28 ॥
1.162.m: A man, though of little means, should do what is impelled by devotion; / even if possessing the essence of great wealth, one should not act destitute of devotion.

1.162.s:
sarvasvamapi yo dadyādarke bhaktivivarjitaḥ ..
na tena dharmabhāgī syādbhaktirevātra kāraṇam .. 29 ..
1.162.d:
सर्वस्वमपि यो दद्यादर्के भक्तिविवर्जितः ॥
न तेन धर्मभागी स्याद्भक्तिरेवात्र कारणम् ॥ 29 ॥
1.162.m: Whoever should give even his entire estate to the Sun destitute of devotion, / he would not partake of righteousness thereby; devotion alone is the cause here.

1.162.s:
na tapobhirvibhorugrairna ca sarvairmahāmakhaiḥ ..
gacchedekaṃ puraṃ divyamarke bhaktiyuto nṛpa .. 1.162.30 ..
1.162.d:
न तपोभिर्विभोरुग्रैर्न च सर्वैर्महामखैः ॥
गच्छेदेकं पुरं दिव्यमर्के भक्तियुतो नृप ॥ 1.162.30 ॥
1.162.m: Not by severe austerities to the Lord, nor by all the great sacrifices, / does one go to the singular divine city, [as one does] when endowed with devotion to the Sun, O king.

1.162.s:
ruciraṃ śubhaśailotthaṃ kuryāyastu ravergṛham ..
trisaptakulasaṃyuktaḥ sūryalokamavāpnuyāt .. 31 ..
1.162.d:
रुचिरं शुभशैलोत्थं कुर्यायस्तु रवेर्गृहम् ॥
त्रिसप्तकुलसंयुक्तः सूर्यलोकमवाप्नुयात् ॥ 31 ॥
1.162.m: Whoever should build a charming house for the Sun out of auspicious stone / would attain the world of the Sun together with twenty-one generations of his family.

1.162.s:
yanmayā koṭiguṇitaṃ kṛtaṃ syādiṣṭakāmyayā ..
dviparārdhaguṇaṃ puṇyaṃ śailaje'pi vidurbudhāḥ .. 32 ..
1.162.d:
यन्मया कोटिगुणितं कृतं स्यादिष्टकाम्यया ॥
द्विपरार्धगुणं पुण्यं शैलजेऽपि विदुर्बुधाः ॥ 32 ॥
1.162.m: What is made of brick brings ten million times [the merit], / and the wise know that [a temple] made of stone brings two parārdhas times the merit.

1.162.s:
mṛcchailena samaṃ jñeyaṃ puṇyamāḍhyadaridrayoḥ ..
yatra tatra gataḥ kuryādbhaktyā puṇyaṃ bhagālayam .. 33 ..
1.162.d:
मृच्छैलेन समं ज्ञेयं पुण्यमाढ्यदरिद्रयोः ॥
यत्र तत्र गतः कुर्याद्भक्त्या पुण्यं भगालयम् ॥ 33 ॥
1.162.m: The merit of the rich and the poor should be understood as equal between clay and stone; / wherever one has gone, one should make with devotion a sacred abode for the Sun.

1.162.s:
śailotthamiṣṭakābhirvā dṛḍhaṃ dārumayaṃ śubham..
sa gacchetparamaṃ sthānaṃ bhānoramitatejasaḥ ..
gairikaṃ yānamāruhya yaḥ kuryāddhṛtabhūṣaṇaḥ .. 34 ..
1.162.d:
शैलोत्थमिष्टकाभिर्वा दृढं दारुमयं शुभम्॥
स गच्छेत्परमं स्थानं भानोरमिततेजसः ॥
गैरिकं यानमारुह्य यः कुर्याद्धृतभूषणः ॥ 34 ॥
1.162.m: Whether made of stone, or of bricks, firm, auspicious, or made of wood, / he who, adorned with ornaments, mounts an ochre chariot and makes it, / would go to the supreme abode of the Sun of boundless splendour.

1.162.s:
krīḍamāno'pi yaḥ kuryādbālabhāve'rkamaṃdiram..
so'rkalokamavāpnoti vimānavaramāsthitaḥ .. 35 ..
1.162.d:
क्रीडमानोऽपि यः कुर्याद्बालभावेऽर्कमंदिरम्॥
सोऽर्कलोकमवाप्नोति विमानवरमास्थितः ॥ 35 ॥
1.162.m: Even playing in childhood, whoever should make a temple for the Sun / reaches the world of the Sun, seated in a superior celestial chariot,

1.162.s:
puṣpamālākulaṃ divyaṃ dhūpagaṃdhādivāsitam ..
apsarogaṇasaṃkīrṇaṃ sarvakāmamukhapradam .. 36 ..
1.162.d:
पुष्पमालाकुलं दिव्यं धूपगंधादिवासितम् ॥
अप्सरोगणसंकीर्णं सर्वकाममुखप्रदम् ॥ 36 ॥
1.162.m: crowded with flower garlands, divine, perfumed with the fragrance of incense, / teeming with hosts of apsarases, granting all desired pleasures.

1.162.s:
tatra rūḍho mahārāja vatsaraṃ vṛndamuttamam ..
uṣitvā bhāskarapure pūjyamānastu daivataiḥ .. 37 ..
1.162.d:
तत्र रूढो महाराज वत्सरं वृन्दमुत्तमम् ॥
उषित्वा भास्करपुरे पूज्यमानस्तु दैवतैः ॥ 37 ॥
1.162.m: Mounted there, O great king, having dwelt for an excellent host of years / in the city of the Sun, being worshipped by the gods,

1.162.s:
kramādāgatya loke'sminrājā bhavati dhārmikaḥ ..
dharmārthakāmasaṃpanno yaśasā ca narādhipa ..38..
1.162.d:
क्रमादागत्य लोकेऽस्मिन्राजा भवति धार्मिकः ॥
धर्मार्थकामसंपन्नो यशसा च नराधिप ॥38॥
1.162.m: having arrived in this world in due course, he becomes a righteous king / endowed with virtue, wealth, and pleasure, and renowned, O lord of men.

1.162.s:
paśyanpariharañjaṃtūnmārjanyā mṛdusūkṣmayā ..
śanaiḥ saṃmārjanaṃ kuryāccāṃdrāyaṇaphalaṃ bhavet ..39..
1.162.d:
पश्यन्परिहरञ्जंतून्मार्जन्या मृदुसूक्ष्मया ॥
शनैः संमार्जनं कुर्याच्चांद्रायणफलं भवेत् ॥39॥
1.162.m: Watching and avoiding small creatures, with a soft and fine broom / one should sweep slowly; that bears the fruit of a cāndrāyaṇa penance.

1.162.s:
putrārthaṃ dehajīrṇāyā vandhyāyāśca viśeṣataḥ ..
rogārtānāṃ ca bhūtānāmārogyārthaṃ prapūjayet .. 1.162.40 ..
1.162.d:
पुत्रार्थं देहजीर्णाया वन्ध्यायाश्च विशेषतः ॥
रोगार्तानां च भूतानामारोग्यार्थं प्रपूजयेत् ॥ 1.162.40 ॥
1.162.m: For the sake of a son for a woman whose body is worn out, and especially for a barren woman, / and for the health of creatures afflicted with disease, one should perform worship.

1.162.s:
gṛhītvā gomayaṃ svacchaṃ sthāne ca patitaṃ śubhe ..
uparyupari saṃtyajya pratyagraṃ jantuvarjitam .. 41 ..
1.162.d:
गृहीत्वा गोमयं स्वच्छं स्थाने च पतितं शुभे ॥
उपर्युपरि संत्यज्य प्रत्यग्रं जन्तुवर्जितम् ॥ 41 ॥
1.162.m: Taking clean cow dung fallen in an auspicious place, / discarding what is on top, [taking it] fresh and free of living creatures,

1.162.s:
vastrapūtagomayena yaḥ kuryādupalepanam ..
paśyettu sukhitāñjaṃtūṃścāṃdrāyaṇaśataṃ labhet .. 42 ..
1.162.d:
वस्त्रपूतगोमयेन यः कुर्यादुपलेपनम् ॥
पश्येत्तु सुखिताञ्जंतूंश्चांद्रायणशतं लभेत् ॥ 42 ॥
1.162.m: he who smears [the floor] with cow dung purified through cloth, / and watches that creatures are kept safe, would obtain the fruit of a hundred cāndrāyaṇas.

1.162.s:
yaḥ kuryātsarvakāryāṇi vastrapūtena vāriṇā ..
sa muniḥ sa mahāsādhuḥ sa gacchetparamāṃ gatim .. 43 ..
1.162.d:
यः कुर्यात्सर्वकार्याणि वस्त्रपूतेन वारिणा ॥
स मुनिः स महासाधुः स गच्छेत्परमां गतिम् ॥ 43 ॥
1.162.m: He who performs all tasks with water purified through cloth / is a sage, he is a great saint, he would go to the supreme state.

1.162.s:
kṣaraṃti sarvadānāni yajñahomabalikriyāḥ ..
akṣaraṃ tu mahādānaṃ sukhadaṃ sarvadehinām .. 44 ..
1.162.d:
क्षरंति सर्वदानानि यज्ञहोमबलिक्रियाः ॥
अक्षरं तु महादानं सुखदं सर्वदेहिनाम् ॥ 44 ॥
1.162.m: All gifts, sacrifices, oblations, and rites of offering perish; / but the imperishable great gift is that which gives happiness to all embodied beings.

1.162.s:
nairaṃtaryeṇa yaḥ kuryātpakṣaṃ saṃmārjanārcanam ..
varṣamekaṃ śataṃ divyaṃ suraloke mahīyate .. 45 ..
1.162.d:
नैरंतर्येण यः कुर्यात्पक्षं संमार्जनार्चनम् ॥
वर्षमेकं शतं दिव्यं सुरलोके महीयते ॥ 45 ॥
1.162.m: Whoever performs sweeping and worship uninterruptedly for a fortnight / is honoured in the world of the gods for a divine hundred years.

1.162.s:
tasyāṃte ca caturveda surūpaḥ priyadarśanaḥ ..
ādyaḥ sarvaguṇopeto rājā bhavati dhārmikaḥ .. 46 ..
1.162.d:
तस्यांते च चतुर्वेद सुरूपः प्रियदर्शनः ॥
आद्यः सर्वगुणोपेतो राजा भवति धार्मिकः ॥ 46 ॥
1.162.m: And at the end of that, he becomes a righteous king, knowing the four Vedas, / handsome, pleasant to behold, foremost, and endowed with all virtues.

1.162.s:
saṃparkeṇāpi yaḥ kuryānnaraḥ karma bhagālaye ..
sopi saumanasaṃ gatvā puraṃ krīḍati nityaśaḥ ..47..
1.162.d:
संपर्केणापि यः कुर्यान्नरः कर्म भगालये ॥
सोपि सौमनसं गत्वा पुरं क्रीडति नित्यशः ॥47॥
1.162.m: Even through mere association, a man who performs work in the temple of the Sun, / having gone to the city of Saumanasa, sports there perpetually.

1.162.s:
tāvadbhramaṃti saṃsāre duḥkhaśokapariplutāḥ ..
na bhajaṃti raviṃ bhaktyā yāvatsarve'pi dehinaḥ .. 48 ..
1.162.d:
तावद्भ्रमंति संसारे दुःखशोकपरिप्लुताः ॥
न भजंति रविं भक्त्या यावत्सर्वेऽपि देहिनः ॥ 48 ॥
1.162.m: So long do all embodied beings wander in saṃsāra, / overwhelmed by pain and grief, as long as they do not worship the Sun with devotion.

1.162.s:
samāsaktaṃ tathā cittaṃ jantorviṣayagocare ..
yadyarko na bhavaddevaḥ ko muñcedeva bandhanāt .. 49 ..
1.162.d:
समासक्तं तथा चित्तं जन्तोर्विषयगोचरे ॥
यद्यर्को न भवद्देवः को मुञ्चेदेव बन्धनात् ॥ 49 ॥
1.162.m: The mind of a creature is so deeply attached to the sphere of sense objects; / if the Sun were not God, who indeed would release it from bondage?

1.162.s:
yaḥ kuryātkuṭṭimāṃ bhūmiṃ darpaṇodarasannibhām ..
nānāvarṇavicitrāṃ ca vicitra kusumojjvalām.. 1.162.50 ..
1.162.d:
यः कुर्यात्कुट्टिमां भूमिं दर्पणोदरसन्निभाम् ॥
नानावर्णविचित्रां च विचित्र कुसुमोज्ज्वलाम्॥ 1.162.50 ॥
1.162.m: Whoever should make the paved ground like the surface of a mirror, / variegated with various colours, and radiant with various flowers,

1.162.s:
kvacitkalaśavinyastāṃ paṃkajairupaśobhitām..
ramyāṃ manoramāṃ saumyāmarkāyatanasaṃsadi .. 51 ..
1.162.d:
क्वचित्कलशविन्यस्तां पंकजैरुपशोभिताम्॥
रम्यां मनोरमां सौम्यामर्कायतनसंसदि ॥ 51 ॥
1.162.m: here and there set with water-jars, adorned with lotuses, / charming, pleasing to the mind, and gentle in the precinct of the temple of the Sun;

1.162.s:
yāvaddaṃḍā bhavedbhūmiḥ samaṃtācca suśobhanā ..
tāvadyugasahasrāṇi sūraloke mahīyate .. 52 ..
1.162.d:
यावद्दंडा भवेद्भूमिः समंताच्च सुशोभना ॥
तावद्युगसहस्राणि सूरलोके महीयते ॥ 52 ॥
1.162.m: for as many staffs [in measure] as the ground is thoroughly beautiful on all sides, / for so many thousands of yugas is he honoured in the world of the Sun.

1.162.s:
kārayeccitraśāstrajñaiścitrakarmārkamaṃdire ..
vicitraṃ yānamāruhya citrabhānorgṛhaṃ vrajet..53..
1.162.d:
कारयेच्चित्रशास्त्रज्ञैश्चित्रकर्मार्कमंदिरे ॥
विचित्रं यानमारुह्य चित्रभानोर्गृहं व्रजेत्॥53॥
1.162.m: One should have painting done in the temple of the Sun by those learned in the science of painting; / mounting a splendid vehicle, he would go to the abode of the Sun.

1.162.s:
yāvatsa devarūpāṇi graharūpāṇi lekhayet ..
tāvadyugasahasrāṇi svargaloke mahīyate .. 54 ..
1.162.d:
यावत्स देवरूपाणि ग्रहरूपाणि लेखयेत् ॥
तावद्युगसहस्राणि स्वर्गलोके महीयते ॥ 54 ॥
1.162.m: For as long as he causes the forms of the gods and the forms of the planets to be painted, / for so many thousands of yugas is he honoured in the world of heaven.

1.162.s:
bhavedbhūmiḥ samaṃtācca yaḥ kuryādarkamaṃdi ram ..
ārāmāvasathādīnāṃ labhedāmūlyakaṃ phalam .. 55 .. ..
sauradharmeṣu puṣpapūjāvarṇanam
1.162.d:
भवेद्भूमिः समंताच्च यः कुर्यादर्कमंदि रम् ॥
आरामावसथादीनां लभेदामूल्यकं फलम् ॥ 55 ॥ ॥
सौरधर्मेषु पुष्पपूजावर्णनम्
1.162.m:
Whoever should construct the ground all around for the temple of the Sun / would obtain the priceless fruit of [giving] pleasure gardens, dwellings, and the like.
Description of the worship with flowers among the duties pertaining to the Sun.

1.163.s:
.. sumanturuvāca .. ..
bhāskarasya mahābāho bhānoramitatejasaḥ ..
snānakāle prakurvīta jayaśabdādimaṃga lam .. 1 ..
1.163.d:
॥ सुमन्तुरुवाच ॥ ॥
भास्करस्य महाबाहो भानोरमिततेजसः ॥
स्नानकाले प्रकुर्वीत जयशब्दादिमंग लम् ॥ 1 ॥
1.163.m:
Sumantu said:
O strong-armed one, at the time of the bath of Bhāskara, the Sun of immeasurable radiance,
one should perform auspicious acts beginning with shouts of victory.

1.163.s:
padmasvastikaśaṃkhaṃ tu śrīvatsaṃ dvijasattama ..
hemarūpādipātreṣu kalpitaṃ gomayādibhiḥ .. 2 ..
1.163.d:
पद्मस्वस्तिकशंखं तु श्रीवत्सं द्विजसत्तम ॥
हेमरूपादिपात्रेषु कल्पितं गोमयादिभिः ॥ 2 ॥
1.163.m:
A lotus, a svastika, a conch, and a śrīvatsa, O best of the twice-born,
fashioned with cow dung and the like upon vessels of gold, silver, and other [metals],

1.163.s:
nānāvarṇakasaṃyuktairakṣataistilataṃdulaiḥ ..
svacchaiśca dadhisaṃmiśrairyathāśobhaṃ prapūritaiḥ .. 3 ..
1.163.d:
नानावर्णकसंयुक्तैरक्षतैस्तिलतंदुलैः ॥
स्वच्छैश्च दधिसंमिश्रैर्यथाशोभं प्रपूरितैः ॥ 3 ॥
1.163.m:
filled as looks most beautiful with whole grains of varied colours,
with sesame seeds and rice grains, pure and mixed with curds;

1.163.s:
dravyapīṭhapradīpāśca bhūtāśvatthādipallavaiḥ ..
auṣadhībhiśca medhyābhiḥ sarvabījairyavādibhiḥ .. .. 4 ..
1.163.d:
द्रव्यपीठप्रदीपाश्च भूताश्वत्थादिपल्लवैः ॥
औषधीभिश्च मेध्याभिः सर्वबीजैर्यवादिभिः ॥ ॥ 4 ॥
1.163.m:
and stands for materials and lamps, with shoots of the sacred fig tree and the like,
with pure medicinal herbs, and with all seeds such as barley.

1.163.s:
saptamyādiṣu sarveṣu ṣaṣṭhyādiṣu viśeṣataḥ ..
śaṃkhabheryādibhiḥ kuryādvādyaghoṣaṃ suśobhanam .. 5 ..
1.163.d:
सप्तम्यादिषु सर्वेषु षष्ठ्यादिषु विशेषतः ॥
शंखभेर्यादिभिः कुर्याद्वाद्यघोषं सुशोभनम् ॥ 5 ॥
1.163.m:
On all [tithis] beginning with the seventh, and especially on those beginning with the sixth,
one should make a beautiful sounding of instruments with conches, kettledrums, and the like.

1.163.s:
trisandhyaṃ vedanirghoṣaṃ kurvīta phalamuttamam ..
kuryānnīrājanaṃ caiva śaṃkhavāditramaṃgalaiḥ .. 6 ..
1.163.d:
त्रिसन्ध्यं वेदनिर्घोषं कुर्वीत फलमुत्तमम् ॥
कुर्यान्नीराजनं चैव शंखवादित्रमंगलैः ॥ 6 ॥
1.163.m:
At the three junctures of the day one should make the resounding of the Vedas, [which yields] the highest fruit,
and one should also perform the waving of lamps with auspicious conches and musical instruments.

1.163.s:
yāvannīrājanaṃ kuryātparvāṇi vidhivadravau ..
tāvadyugasahasrāṇi sūraloke mahīyate .. 7 ..
1.163.d:
यावन्नीराजनं कुर्यात्पर्वाणि विधिवद्रवौ ॥
तावद्युगसहस्राणि सूरलोके महीयते ॥ 7 ॥
1.163.m:
For as long as one performs the waving of lamps to the Sun on festival days according to rule,
for so many thousands of yugas he is glorified in the world of the Sun.

1.163.s:
kapilāpañcagavyena kuśavāriyutena vai ..
snāpayenmantrapūtena brahmasnānaṃ hi tatsmṛtam .. 8 ..
1.163.d:
कपिलापञ्चगव्येन कुशवारियुतेन वै ॥
स्नापयेन्मन्त्रपूतेन ब्रह्मस्नानं हि तत्स्मृतम् ॥ 8 ॥
1.163.m:
With the five cow-products of a brown cow mixed with kuśa-water
one should bathe [him], purified with mantras; that is indeed considered the Brahma-bath.

1.163.s:
yastvekamapi sarvebde brahmasnānaṃ prayacchati ..
sa muktaḥ sarvapāpaistu sūryaloke mahīyate .. 9 ..
1.163.d:
यस्त्वेकमपि सर्वेब्दे ब्रह्मस्नानं प्रयच्छति ॥
स मुक्तः सर्वपापैस्तु सूर्यलोके महीयते ॥ 9 ॥
1.163.m:
He who offers even a single Brahma-bath in an entire year
is freed from all sins and glorified in the world of the Sun.

1.163.s:
kapilāpañcagavyena dadhikṣīrayutena ca ..
snānaṃ daśaguṇaṃ jñeyaṃ mahatpuṇyaṃ narādhipa .. 1.163.10 ..
1.163.d:
कपिलापञ्चगव्येन दधिक्षीरयुतेन च ॥
स्नानं दशगुणं ज्ञेयं महत्पुण्यं नराधिप ॥ 1.163.10 ॥
1.163.m:
A bath with the five cow-products of a brown cow accompanied by curd and milk
is known to have tenfold [potency], a great merit, O lord of men.

1.163.s:
ṛbhavo vīramuddiśya dehaśuddhiṃ ca śāśvatīm ..
kapilāmāharennityaṃ munidevāgninirmitām .. 11 ..
1.163.d:
ऋभवो वीरमुद्दिश्य देहशुद्धिं च शाश्वतीम् ॥
कपिलामाहरेन्नित्यं मुनिदेवाग्निनिर्मिताम् ॥ 11 ॥
1.163.m:
For the sake of a hero and for eternal bodily purification,
one should constantly fetch the brown cow, fashioned by sages, gods, and fire, as the Ṛbhus did.

1.163.s:
kāpilaṃ yaḥ pibecchūdro devakāryārthanirmitam ..
sa pacyate mahāghore suciraṃ narakārṇave .. 12 ..
1.163.d:
कापिलं यः पिबेच्छूद्रो देवकार्यार्थनिर्मितम् ॥
स पच्यते महाघोरे सुचिरं नरकार्णवे ॥ 12 ॥
1.163.m:
Whatever Śūdra drinks the [milk] of a brown cow prepared for the rites of the gods
is boiled for a very long time in the dreadful ocean of hell.

1.163.s:
varṣakoṭisahasreṇa yatpāpaṃ samupārjitam ..
ghṛtābhyaṃgena sūryasya dahetsarvaṃ na saṃśayaḥ .. 13 ..
1.163.d:
वर्षकोटिसहस्रेण यत्पापं समुपार्जितम् ॥
घृताभ्यंगेन सूर्यस्य दहेत्सर्वं न संशयः ॥ 13 ॥
1.163.m:
Whatever sin has been accumulated through thousands of crores of years,
he burns it all away through anointing the Sun with ghee; there is no doubt.

1.163.s:
kalpakoṭisahasraistu yatpāpaṃ samupārjitam ..
vajrasnānena tatsarvaṃ dahatyagniriveṃdhanam .. 14 ..
1.163.d:
कल्पकोटिसहस्रैस्तु यत्पापं समुपार्जितम् ॥
वज्रस्नानेन तत्सर्वं दहत्यग्निरिवेंधनम् ॥ 14 ॥
1.163.m:
Whatever sin has been accumulated through thousands of crores of aeons,
he burns it all away through the diamond-bath, as fire burns fuel.

1.163.s:
saptamyāṃ ca kṛtasnāno yajetsūryaṃ sakṛnnaraḥ ..
kulānyuddhṛtya sapteha sūryaloke mahīyate ..
vasuhemādiyuktaṃ ca kṣīrasnānasya tatsamam .. 15 ..
1.163.d:
सप्तम्यां च कृतस्नानो यजेत्सूर्यं सकृन्नरः ॥
कुलान्युद्धृत्य सप्तेह सूर्यलोके महीयते ॥
वसुहेमादियुक्तं च क्षीरस्नानस्य तत्समम् ॥ 15 ॥

1.163.s:
sakṛdāḍhakena payasā yo bhānuṃ snāpa yennaraḥ ..
rājatena vimānena so'rkaloke mahīyate .. 16 ..
1.163.d:
सकृदाढकेन पयसा यो भानुं स्नाप येन्नरः ॥
राजतेन विमानेन सोऽर्कलोके महीयते ॥ 16 ॥
1.163.m:
A man who bathes the Sun even once with an āḍhaka measure of milk
is glorified in the world of the Sun on a silver celestial chariot.

1.163.s:
snāpya dadhnā sakṛdbhānuṃ sa triloke mahīyate ..
madhunā snapayitvā taṃ śukraloke mahī yate .. 17 ..
1.163.d:
स्नाप्य दध्ना सकृद्भानुं स त्रिलोके महीयते ॥
मधुना स्नपयित्वा तं शुक्रलोके मही यते ॥ 17 ॥
1.163.m:
Having bathed the Sun once with curd, he is glorified in the three worlds;
having bathed him with honey, he is glorified in the world of Śukra.

1.163.s:
uddhṛtya śālipiṣṭena vāyulokeṣu pūjyate ..
snānamikṣuraseneha yaḥ sūrye sakṛdācaret ..
sa gopatipuraṃ gacchetsarvakāmasamanvitaḥ .. .. 18 ..
1.163.d:
उद्धृत्य शालिपिष्टेन वायुलोकेषु पूज्यते ॥
स्नानमिक्षुरसेनेह यः सूर्ये सकृदाचरेत् ॥
स गोपतिपुरं गच्छेत्सर्वकामसमन्वितः ॥ ॥ 18 ॥
1.163.m:
Rubbing him with rice flour, he is worshipped in the worlds of Vāyu.
He who performs a bath for the Sun with sugarcane juice even once in this world
goes to the city of the lord of cattle, endowed with all desires.

1.163.s:
phalodakena yo bhānuṃ sakṛtsnāpayate naraḥ ..
utsṛjya pāpakalilaṃ pitṛloke mahīyate .. 19 ..
1.163.d:
फलोदकेन यो भानुं सकृत्स्नापयते नरः ॥
उत्सृज्य पापकलिलं पितृलोके महीयते ॥ 19 ॥
1.163.m:
A man who bathes the Sun even once with fruit-water,
casting off the stain of sin, is glorified in the world of the ancestors.

1.163.s:
śrīkhaṃḍavāriṇā snāpya sakṛdbhānuṃ narā dhipa ..
caṃdrāṃśunirmalaḥ śrīmāṃścaredātreyamaṃdire .. 1.163.20 ..
1.163.d:
श्रीखंडवारिणा स्नाप्य सकृद्भानुं नरा धिप ॥
चंद्रांशुनिर्मलः श्रीमांश्चरेदात्रेयमंदिरे ॥ 1.163.20 ॥
1.163.m:
Having bathed the Sun once with sandalwood water, O lord of men,
he wanders in the abode of the moon, radiant and pure as moonbeams.

1.163.s:
vastrapūtena toyena yadyarkaṃ snāpayetsakṛt ..
sa sarvakāmatṛptātmā rākādhipapuraṃ vrajet ..21..
1.163.d:
वस्त्रपूतेन तोयेन यद्यर्कं स्नापयेत्सकृत् ॥
स सर्वकामतृप्तात्मा राकाधिपपुरं व्रजेत् ॥21॥
1.163.m:
If he should bathe the Sun even once with water purified with a cloth,
with his soul fulfilled of all desires, he goes to the city of the lord of the full-moon night.

1.163.s:
āpo hiṣṭheti japyena gaṃgātoyena bhārata ..
gairikeṇa vimānena brahmaloke mahīyate .. 22 ..
1.163.d:
आपो हिष्ठेति जप्येन गंगातोयेन भारत ॥
गैरिकेण विमानेन ब्रह्मलोके महीयते ॥ 22 ॥
1.163.m:
With Gaṅgā water while reciting the prayer 'āpo hi ṣṭhā', O descendant of Bharata,
he is glorified in the world of Brahmā upon a red-chalk celestial chariot.

1.163.s:
karpūrāgurutoyena yo'rkaṃ snāpayate sakṛt ..
snāpya bhānuṃ sakṛnmantraiḥ saptamyāṃ samupoṣitaḥ ..
sa kulānekaviṃśatimuttārya ravimāvrajet .. 23 ..
1.163.d:
कर्पूरागुरुतोयेन योऽर्कं स्नापयते सकृत् ॥
स्नाप्य भानुं सकृन्मन्त्रैः सप्तम्यां समुपोषितः ॥
स कुलानेकविंशतिमुत्तार्य रविमाव्रजेत् ॥ 23 ॥
1.163.m:
He who bathes the Sun even once with camphor and agallochum water,
having bathed the Sun once with mantras while fasting on the seventh [lunar day],
uplifts twenty-one generations and reaches the Sun.

1.163.s:
pitṛnuddiśya yo bhānuṃ snāpayecchītavāriṇā ..
tṛptāḥ svarga vrajaṃtyāśu pitaro narakādapi .. 24 ..
1.163.d:
पितृनुद्दिश्य यो भानुं स्नापयेच्छीतवारिणा ॥
तृप्ताः स्वर्ग व्रजंत्याशु पितरो नरकादपि ॥ 24 ॥
1.163.m:
He who bathes the Sun with cool water on behalf of the ancestors—
the ancestors, being satisfied, go swiftly to heaven even from hell.

1.163.s:
bhānuṃ śītāṃbunā snāpya dhāroṣṇapayasā saha ..
snāpya paścādvrateneśamagniloke mahīyate .. 25 ..
1.163.d:
भानुं शीतांबुना स्नाप्य धारोष्णपयसा सह ॥
स्नाप्य पश्चाद्व्रतेनेशमग्निलोके महीयते ॥ 25 ॥
1.163.m:
Having bathed the Sun with cool water together with milk fresh from the udder,
and having then bathed the Lord according to the rite, he is glorified in the world of Fire.

1.163.s:
etatsnānatrayaṃ kṛtvā pūjayitvā tu bhārata ..
aśvamedhasahasrasya phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ .. 26 ..
1.163.d:
एतत्स्नानत्रयं कृत्वा पूजयित्वा तु भारत ॥
अश्वमेधसहस्रस्य फलं प्राप्नोति मानवः ॥ 26 ॥
1.163.m:
Having performed these three baths and worshipped [him], O descendant of Bharata,
a man attains the fruit of a thousand horse sacrifices.

1.163.s:
mṛtkumbhāttāmrakumbhaistu snānaṃ śataguṇaṃ matam ..
raupyaiḥ pādottaraṃ puṇyaṃ darśanātsparśanaṃ param ..
sparśanādarcanaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ ghṛtasnānamataḥ param .. 27 ..
1.163.d:
मृत्कुम्भात्ताम्रकुम्भैस्तु स्नानं शतगुणं मतम् ॥
रौप्यैः पादोत्तरं पुण्यं दर्शनात्स्पर्शनं परम् ॥
स्पर्शनादर्चनं श्रेष्ठं घृतस्नानमतः परम् ॥ 27 ॥

1.163.s:
ihāmutra kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ ghṛtasnānena naśyati ..
saptajanma kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ purāṇaśravaṇena tu ..28..
1.163.d:
इहामुत्र कृतं पापं घृतस्नानेन नश्यति ॥
सप्तजन्म कृतं पापं पुराणश्रवणेन तु ॥28॥
1.163.m:
Sin committed in this world and the next is destroyed by a bath of ghee;
and sin committed in seven births is destroyed by hearing the Purāṇa.

1.163.s:
daśāparādhāṃstoyena kṣīreṇa tu śataṃ kṣamet ..
sahasraṃ kṣamate dadhnā ghṛtenāpyayutaṃ kṣamet ..29..
1.163.d:
दशापराधांस्तोयेन क्षीरेण तु शतं क्षमेत् ॥
सहस्रं क्षमते दध्ना घृतेनाप्ययुतं क्षमेत् ॥29॥
1.163.m:
He forgives ten offences with water, but a hundred with milk;
he forgives a thousand with curd, and ten thousand with ghee.

1.163.s:
nairantaryeṇa yo māsaṃ ghṛtasnānaṃ samācaret ..
daśaikādaśa kulānīha nayetsūryasya maṃdiram .. 1.163.30 ..
1.163.d:
नैरन्तर्येण यो मासं घृतस्नानं समाचरेत् ॥
दशैकादश कुलानीह नयेत्सूर्यस्य मंदिरम् ॥ 1.163.30 ॥
1.163.m:
He who performs the bath of ghee continuously for a month
leads twenty-one ancestral lines to the abode of the Sun.

1.163.s:
snānaṃ palaśataṃ jñeyamabhyaṃgaḥ pañcaviṃśatiḥ ..
palānāṃ dvisahasreṇa mahāsnānamati śrutiḥ..31..
1.163.d:
स्नानं पलशतं ज्ञेयमभ्यंगः पञ्चविंशतिः ॥
पलानां द्विसहस्रेण महास्नानमति श्रुतिः॥31॥
1.163.m:
A bath is known to be one hundred palas; an anointing is twenty-five;
with two thousand palas it is a great bath, according to tradition.

1.163.s:
ghṛtābhyaṃgaṃ ghṛtasnāna bhānoḥ kuryyāddvijottama..
yaśca godhūmacūrṇaistu kaṣāyairdarbhasaṃmitaiḥ..32 ..
1.163.d:
घृताभ्यंगं घृतस्नान भानोः कुर्य्याद्द्विजोत्तम॥
यश्च गोधूमचूर्णैस्तु कषायैर्दर्भसंमितैः॥32 ॥
1.163.m:
O best of the twice-born, one should perform the ghee-anointing and ghee-bath of the Sun;
and he who [does so] with wheat flours and decoctions prepared with darbha grass,

1.163.s:
daśadhenusahasrāṇi yaddattvā labhate phalam..
tatphalaṃ labhate sarvamarkasyodvartane kṛte..33..
1.163.d:
दशधेनुसहस्राणि यद्दत्त्वा लभते फलम्॥
तत्फलं लभते सर्वमर्कस्योद्वर्तने कृते॥33॥
1.163.m:
whatever fruit one obtains by giving ten thousand milch cows,
all that fruit one obtains when an unction of the Sun is performed.

1.163.s:
arghyaṃ puṣpaphalopetaṃ yastvarkāya nivedayet..
sa pūjyaḥ sarvalokeṣu arkavanmodate divi..34..
1.163.d:
अर्घ्यं पुष्पफलोपेतं यस्त्वर्काय निवेदयेत्॥
स पूज्यः सर्वलोकेषु अर्कवन्मोदते दिवि॥34॥
1.163.m:
He who offers an arghya endowed with flowers and fruits to the Sun
is worthy of worship in all the worlds and rejoices like the Sun in heaven.

1.163.s:
gaṃdhatoyena saṃmiśramudakāddvādaśottaram ..
pañcagavyasamāyuktamarghyaṃ śataguṇaṃ nṛpa .. 35 ..
1.163.d:
गंधतोयेन संमिश्रमुदकाद्द्वादशोत्तरम् ॥
पञ्चगव्यसमायुक्तमर्घ्यं शतगुणं नृप ॥ 35 ॥
1.163.m:
An arghya mixed with fragrant water is twelve times greater than one of water;
combined with the five cow-products it is a hundredfold, O king.

1.163.s:
yoṣṭāṃgagarbhamāpūrya bhānormūrdhni nivedayet ..
daśavarṣasahasrāṇi ramate cārkamaṃdire .. 36 ..
1.163.d:
योष्टांगगर्भमापूर्य भानोर्मूर्ध्नि निवेदयेत् ॥
दशवर्षसहस्राणि रमते चार्कमंदिरे ॥ 36 ॥
1.163.m:
He who, having filled the eight-limbed womb, offers it upon the head of the Sun,
rejoices in the abode of the Sun for ten thousand years.

1.163.s:
āpaḥ kṣīraṃ kuśāgrāṇi ghṛtaṃ dadhi tathā madhu ..
raktāni karavīrāṇi tathā raktaṃ ca canda nam .. 37 ..
1.163.d:
आपः क्षीरं कुशाग्राणि घृतं दधि तथा मधु ॥
रक्तानि करवीराणि तथा रक्तं च चन्द नम् ॥ 37 ॥
1.163.m:
Water, milk, tips of kuśa grass, ghee, curd, and honey,
red oleanders, and red sandalwood—

1.163.s:
aṣṭāṃga eṣa argho vai brahmaṇā parikīrtitaḥ ..
satataṃ prītijanano bhāskarasya narādhipa .. 38 ..
1.163.d:
अष्टांग एष अर्घो वै ब्रह्मणा परिकीर्तितः ॥
सततं प्रीतिजननो भास्करस्य नराधिप ॥ 38 ॥
1.163.m:
this is indeed declared by Brahmā to be the eightfold arghya;
it perpetually produces the delight of Bhāskara, O lord of men.

1.163.s:
dāturvaiṇavapātreṇa datte'rghye yatphalaṃ bhavet ..
tasmācchataguṇaṃ puṇyaṃ mṛtpātreṇa narādhipa .. 39 ..
1.163.d:
दातुर्वैणवपात्रेण दत्तेऽर्घ्ये यत्फलं भवेत् ॥
तस्माच्छतगुणं पुण्यं मृत्पात्रेण नराधिप ॥ 39 ॥
1.163.m:
Whatever fruit there may be for the giver when an arghya is given with a bamboo vessel,
the merit is a hundred times that with an earthen vessel, O lord of men.

1.163.s:
tāmrārghyapātradānena puṇyaṃ śataguṇaṃ matam ..
pālāśapadmapatrābhyāṃ tāmrapātre phalaṃ labhet .. 1.163.40 ..
1.163.d:
ताम्रार्घ्यपात्रदानेन पुण्यं शतगुणं मतम् ॥
पालाशपद्मपत्राभ्यां ताम्रपात्रे फलं लभेत् ॥ 1.163.40 ॥
1.163.m:
The merit is considered a hundredfold by the gift of a copper arghya-vessel;
with palāśa and lotus leaves one obtains the fruit of a copper vessel.

1.163.s:
raupyapātreṇa vijñeyaṃ lakṣārghyaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ ..
suvarṇapātravinyastamarghyaṃ koṭiguṇaṃ bhavet .. 41 ..
1.163.d:
रौप्यपात्रेण विज्ञेयं लक्षार्घ्यं नात्र संशयः ॥
सुवर्णपात्रविन्यस्तमर्घ्यं कोटिगुणं भवेत् ॥ 41 ॥
1.163.m:
With a silver vessel it is known to be a hundred thousand arghyas; there is no doubt of this;
an arghya placed in a golden vessel becomes ten-million-fold.

1.163.s:
evaṃ snānārghyanaivedyabalidhūpādiṣu kramāt ..
pātrāṃtaraviśeṣeṇa tatphalaṃ tūttarottaram .. 42 ..
1.163.d:
एवं स्नानार्घ्यनैवेद्यबलिधूपादिषु क्रमात् ॥
पात्रांतरविशेषेण तत्फलं तूत्तरोत्तरम् ॥ 42 ॥
1.163.m:
Thus, in the bath, arghya, food offerings, oblations, incense, and so forth, in order,
the fruit becomes progressively greater according to the distinction among the vessels.

1.163.s:
raupyapātrapradānena yatpuṇyaṃ vedapārage ..
tāmrapātrapradānena tasmācchataguṇaṃ ravau .. .. 43 ..
1.163.d:
रौप्यपात्रप्रदानेन यत्पुण्यं वेदपारगे ॥
ताम्रपात्रप्रदानेन तस्माच्छतगुणं रवौ ॥ ॥ 43 ॥
1.163.m:
Whatever merit comes from the gift of a silver vessel to one who has mastered the Vedas,
that [which comes] from the gift of a copper vessel to the Sun is a hundred times greater than that.

1.163.s:
phalaṃ koṭisuvarṇasya yo dadyādvedapārage ..
sūryāya rūpyapātre tu bhavetpuṇyaṃ tato'dhikam ..44..
1.163.d:
फलं कोटिसुवर्णस्य यो दद्याद्वेदपारगे ॥
सूर्याय रूप्यपात्रे तु भवेत्पुण्यं ततोऽधिकम् ॥44॥
1.163.m: The merit from giving ten million gold coins to one who has crossed the Veda, / is surpassed by that of [giving] a silver vessel to the Sun.

1.163.s:
suvarṇapātraṃ yo dadyādbhāskarāya mahīpate ..
na śakyaṃ tasya tadvaktuṃ puṇyaṃ pātraviśeṣataḥ .. 45 ..
1.163.d:
सुवर्णपात्रं यो दद्याद्भास्कराय महीपते ॥
न शक्यं तस्य तद्वक्तुं पुण्यं पात्रविशेषतः ॥ 45 ॥
1.163.m: O king, the merit of one who presents a gold vessel to the Sun / cannot be told, owing to the superior vessel.

1.163.s:
tulyameva phalaṃ proktaṃ sarvamāḍhyadaridrayoḥ ..
tayorabhyadhikaṃ tasya yastvarke bhāvanādhikaḥ .. .. 46 ..
1.163.d:
तुल्यमेव फलं प्रोक्तं सर्वमाढ्यदरिद्रयोः ॥
तयोरभ्यधिकं तस्य यस्त्वर्के भावनाधिकः ॥ ॥ 46 ॥
1.163.m: The reward is said to be entirely equal for the rich and the poor; / between the two, greater is his who excels in devotion toward the Sun.

1.163.s:
vibhave sati yo mohānna kuryādvidhivistaram ..
naiva tatphalamāpnoti pralobhākrāṃtamānasaḥ .. 47 ..
1.163.d:
विभवे सति यो मोहान्न कुर्याद्विधिविस्तरम् ॥
नैव तत्फलमाप्नोति प्रलोभाक्रांतमानसः ॥ 47 ॥
1.163.m: When one possesses wealth yet fails through delusion to perform the full ritual detail, / he whose mind is overcome with greed does not attain that reward at all.

1.163.s:
tasmānmantraiḥ phalaistoyaiścandanādyaiśca yatnataḥ ..
tadanaṃtaphalaṃ jñeyaṃ bhaktirevātra kāraṇam .. 48 ..
1.163.d:
तस्मान्मन्त्रैः फलैस्तोयैश्चन्दनाद्यैश्च यत्नतः ॥
तदनंतफलं ज्ञेयं भक्तिरेवात्र कारणम् ॥ 48 ॥
1.163.m: Therefore, by mantras, fruits, waters, sandal, and the like, offered with care, / that [fruit] is known to be endless; devotion alone is the cause here.

1.163.s:
varṣakoṭiśataṃ divyaṃ sūryaloke mahīyate ..
gaṃdhānulepanaṃ puṇyaṃ dviguṇaṃ candanasya tu .. .. 49 ..
1.163.d:
वर्षकोटिशतं दिव्यं सूर्यलोके महीयते ॥
गंधानुलेपनं पुण्यं द्विगुणं चन्दनस्य तु ॥ ॥ 49 ॥
1.163.m: One is honoured in the realm of the Sun for a hundred celestial crores of years. / The merit of anointing with fragrant perfume is double that of sandalwood.

1.163.s:
gaṃdhāccaturguṇaṃ jñeyaṃ puṣpamaṣṭaguṇaṃ nṛpa ..
kṛṣṇāguru viśeṣeṇa dviguṇaṃ phalamādiśeta ..
tasmācchataguṇaṃ puṇyaṃ kuṃkumasya vidhīyate .. 1.163.50 ...
1.163.d:
गंधाच्चतुर्गुणं ज्ञेयं पुष्पमष्टगुणं नृप ॥
कृष्णागुरु विशेषेण द्विगुणं फलमादिशेत ॥
तस्माच्छतगुणं पुण्यं कुंकुमस्य विधीयते ॥ 1.163.50 ॥।
1.163.m: Four times that of fragrance is flowers, O king, known to be eightfold. / Black aloe-wood in particular yields twice the fruit; / a hundred times greater than that is prescribed as the merit of saffron.

1.163.s:
caṃdanāgurukarpūraiḥ ślakṣṇapiṣṭaiḥ sakuṃkumaiḥ ..
bhānuṃ paryāptamālipya kalpakoṭiṃ vaseddivi .. 51 ..
1.163.d:
चंदनागुरुकर्पूरैः श्लक्ष्णपिष्टैः सकुंकुमैः ॥
भानुं पर्याप्तमालिप्य कल्पकोटिं वसेद्दिवि ॥ 51 ॥
1.163.m: Smearing the Sun amply with finely ground sandalwood, aloe-wood, / camphor, and saffron, one dwells in heaven for a crore of kalpas.

1.163.s:
sa dīvyetsuravṛndena puṇyagaṃdhaiḥ pralepitaḥ ..
daśavarṣasahasrāṇi vīra mitrapure vaset .. 52 ..
1.163.d:
स दीव्येत्सुरवृन्देन पुण्यगंधैः प्रलेपितः ॥
दशवर्षसहस्राणि वीर मित्रपुरे वसेत् ॥ 52 ॥
1.163.m: Anointed with fragrant unguents, he sports with the host of gods. / For ten thousand years, O hero, he dwells in the city of Mitra.

1.163.s:
bhaktyā nivedya arkāya tālavṛṃtaṃ narādhipa ..
daśavarṣasahasrāṇi vīralokaṃ mahīyate .. 53 ..
1.163.d:
भक्त्या निवेद्य अर्काय तालवृंतं नराधिप ॥
दशवर्षसहस्राणि वीरलोकं महीयते ॥ 53 ॥
1.163.m: Offering a palm-leaf fan with devotion to the Sun, O king, / one is honoured in the world of heroes for ten thousand years.

1.163.s:
māyūraṃ vyajanaṃ dattvā sūryāyātīva śobhanam ..
varṣakoṭiśataṃ pūrṇaṃ prabhaṃjanapure vaset .. 54 ..
1.163.d:
मायूरं व्यजनं दत्त्वा सूर्यायातीव शोभनम् ॥
वर्षकोटिशतं पूर्णं प्रभंजनपुरे वसेत् ॥ 54 ॥
1.163.m: Having offered an exceedingly splendid fan of peacock feathers to the Sun, / one dwells in the city of the Wind God for a full hundred crores of years.

1.163.s:
puṣpairaraṇyasaṃbhūtaiḥ patrairvā girisambhavaiḥ ..
aparyuṣitaniśchidraiḥ proṣitairjaṃtuvarjitaiḥ .. 55 ..
1.163.d:
पुष्पैररण्यसंभूतैः पत्रैर्वा गिरिसम्भवैः ॥
अपर्युषितनिश्छिद्रैः प्रोषितैर्जंतुवर्जितैः ॥ 55 ॥
1.163.m: With flowers born in the forest, or leaves sprung from mountains, / that are not stale, are unpierced, gathered fresh, and free from vermin,

1.163.s:
ātmārāmabhavaiścaiva puṣpaiḥ saṃpūjayedravim ..
puṣpajātiviśeṣeṇa bhavetpuṇyaṃ tato'dhikam .. 56 ..
1.163.d:
आत्मारामभवैश्चैव पुष्पैः संपूजयेद्रविम् ॥
पुष्पजातिविशेषेण भवेत्पुण्यं ततोऽधिकम् ॥ 56 ॥
1.163.m: and also with flowers grown in one's own garden, one should worship the Sun; / and through the distinction of the species of flower, the merit becomes greater still.

1.163.s:
tapaḥśīlaguṇopeta iti hāsavidi dvije ..
dattvā daśa suvarṇasya niṣkānyallabhate phalam .. 57 ..
1.163.d:
तपःशीलगुणोपेत इति हासविदि द्विजे ॥
दत्त्वा दश सुवर्णस्य निष्कान्यल्लभते फलम् ॥ 57 ॥
1.163.m: The reward one attains by giving ten golden niṣkas / to a twice-born endowed with asceticism and virtue, who knows the Itihāsas,

1.163.s:
karavīrasya kusumamarkāya vinivedayet ..
labhate tatphalaṃ vīra yathāha bhagavānraviḥ ..
evaṃ puṣpaviśeṣeṇa phalaṃ tadadhikaṃ bhavet ..
jñeyaṃ puṇyaṃ rasajñena yathā syāttannibodha me .. 58 ..
1.163.d:
करवीरस्य कुसुममर्काय विनिवेदयेत् ॥
लभते तत्फलं वीर यथाह भगवान्रविः ॥
एवं पुष्पविशेषेण फलं तदधिकं भवेत् ॥
ज्ञेयं पुण्यं रसज्ञेन यथा स्यात्तन्निबोध मे ॥ 58 ॥
1.163.m: that reward one obtains by offering a karavīra flower to the Sun, / O hero, just as the blessed Sun has said. / Thus, by the excellence of the flower, the reward becomes greater; / learn from me how the merit is to be known by one discerning of essences.

1.163.s:
sadā puṣpasahasrebhyaḥ karavīraṃ viśiṣyate ..
bilvapatrasahasrebhyaḥ padmamekaṃ narādhipa.. 59 ..
1.163.d:
सदा पुष्पसहस्रेभ्यः करवीरं विशिष्यते ॥
बिल्वपत्रसहस्रेभ्यः पद्ममेकं नराधिप॥ 59 ॥
1.163.m: A karavīra is always superior to a thousand flowers; / a single lotus is superior to a thousand bilva leaves, O king.

1.163.s:
padmapuṣpasahasrebhyo bakapuṣpaṃ viśiṣyate ..
bakapuṣpasahasrebhyo mudgaraṃ paramucyate..1.163.60..
1.163.d:
पद्मपुष्पसहस्रेभ्यो बकपुष्पं विशिष्यते ॥
बकपुष्पसहस्रेभ्यो मुद्गरं परमुच्यते॥1.163.60॥
1.163.m: A baka flower is superior to a thousand lotus flowers; / a mudgara flower is declared supreme over a thousand baka flowers.

1.163.s:
kuśapuṣpasahasrebhyaḥ śamīpatraṃ viśiṣyate ..
śamīpuṣpasahasrebhyo nṛpa nīlotpalaṃ param ..
sarvāsāṃ puṣpajātīnāṃ pravaraṃ nīlamutpalam .. 61 ..
1.163.d:
कुशपुष्पसहस्रेभ्यः शमीपत्रं विशिष्यते ॥
शमीपुष्पसहस्रेभ्यो नृप नीलोत्पलं परम् ॥
सर्वासां पुष्पजातीनां प्रवरं नीलमुत्पलम् ॥ 61 ॥
1.163.m: A śamī leaf is superior to a thousand kuśa flowers; / a blue water-lily is supreme over a thousand śamī flowers, O king. / The blue water-lily is the best among all species of flowers.

1.163.s:
raktotpalasahasreṇa nīlotpalaśatena ca ..
raktaiśca karavīraiśca yastu pūjayate ravim .. 62 ..
1.163.d:
रक्तोत्पलसहस्रेण नीलोत्पलशतेन च ॥
रक्तैश्च करवीरैश्च यस्तु पूजयते रविम् ॥ 62 ॥
1.163.m: He who worships the Sun with a thousand red water-lilies, / a hundred blue water-lilies, and red karavīras,

1.163.s:
kalpakoṭisahasrāṇi kalpakoṭiśatāni ca ..
vasedarkapure śrīmānsūryatulyaparākramaḥ .. 63 ..
1.163.d:
कल्पकोटिसहस्राणि कल्पकोटिशतानि च ॥
वसेदर्कपुरे श्रीमान्सूर्यतुल्यपराक्रमः ॥ 63 ॥
1.163.m: dwells in the city of the Sun for thousands of crores of kalpas / and hundreds of crores of kalpas, glorious and equal in valour to the Sun.

1.163.s:
śeṣāṇāṃ puṣpajātīnāṃ yatphalaṃ parikīrtitam ..
tatphalasyānusāreṇa sūryaloke mahīyate .. 64 ..
1.163.d:
शेषाणां पुष्पजातीनां यत्फलं परिकीर्तितम् ॥
तत्फलस्यानुसारेण सूर्यलोके महीयते ॥ 64 ॥
1.163.m: Whatever reward has been proclaimed for the remaining species of flowers, / in accordance with that reward, he is honoured in the realm of the Sun.

1.163.s:
śamīpuṣpaṃ bṛhatyāśca kusumaṃ tulyamucyate ..
karavīrasamā jñeyā jātīvijayapāṭalāḥ.. 65 ..
1.163.d:
शमीपुष्पं बृहत्याश्च कुसुमं तुल्यमुच्यते ॥
करवीरसमा ज्ञेया जातीविजयपाटलाः॥ 65 ॥
1.163.m: The śamī flower and the flower of the bṛhatī are declared to be equal; / jātī, vijayā, and pāṭalā are known to be equal to the karavīra.

1.163.s:
śvetamaṃdārakusumaṃ sitapuṣpaṃ ca tatsamam ..
nalacaṃpakapunnāgamudgarāṇāṃ samāḥ smṛtāḥ .. 66 ..
1.163.d:
श्वेतमंदारकुसुमं सितपुष्पं च तत्समम् ॥
नलचंपकपुन्नागमुद्गराणां समाः स्मृताः ॥ 66 ॥
1.163.m: The white mandāra flower and the sitapuṣpa are its equal; / [and they are] considered equal to nala, campaka, punnāga, and mudgara.

1.163.s:
gaṃdhavaṃtyapavitrāṇi kusumāni vivarjayet ..
gaṃdhahīnamapi grāhyaṃ pavitraṃ yatkuśādikam .. 67 ..
1.163.d:
गंधवंत्यपवित्राणि कुसुमानि विवर्जयेत् ॥
गंधहीनमपि ग्राह्यं पवित्रं यत्कुशादिकम् ॥ 67 ॥
1.163.m: One should avoid flowers that are fragrant but impure; / even what is devoid of fragrance, if pure, like kuśa grass and the like, is acceptable.

1.163.s:
sāttvikaṃ taddhi kusumamapavitraṃ ca tāmasam ..
mudgarāṇi kadaṃbāni rātrau deyāni sūraye .. 68 ..
1.163.d:
सात्त्विकं तद्धि कुसुममपवित्रं च तामसम् ॥
मुद्गराणि कदंबानि रात्रौ देयानि सूरये ॥ 68 ॥
1.163.m: For that flower is sattvic, while the impure is tamasic. / Mudgaras and kadambas are to be given to the Sun at night.

1.163.s:
divāśeṣāṇi puṣpāṇi tyajedupahatāni ca ..
mukulairmārcayedbhānumapakvaṃ na nivedayet .. 69 ..
1.163.d:
दिवाशेषाणि पुष्पाणि त्यजेदुपहतानि च ॥
मुकुलैर्मार्चयेद्भानुमपक्वं न निवेदयेत् ॥ 69 ॥
1.163.m: The rest of the flowers [are given] by day, and one should discard damaged ones. / One must not worship the Sun with buds, nor offer what is unripe.

1.163.s:
phalaṃ kvathitaviddhaṃ ca yatnātpakvamapi tyajet ..
alābhe bata puṣpāṇāṃ patrāṇyapi nivedayet .. 1.163.70 ..
1.163.d:
फलं क्वथितविद्धं च यत्नात्पक्वमपि त्यजेत् ॥
अलाभे बत पुष्पाणां पत्राण्यपि निवेदयेत् ॥ 1.163.70 ॥
1.163.m: Fruit that is boiled or worm-eaten, even if ripe, should be carefully avoided. / If flowers are unavailable, one may indeed offer leaves.

1.163.s:
patrāṇāmapyalābhe tu phalānyapi nivedayet ..
phalānāmapyalābhena tṛṇagulmauṣadhīrapi .. 71..
1.163.d:
पत्राणामप्यलाभे तु फलान्यपि निवेदयेत् ॥
फलानामप्यलाभेन तृणगुल्मौषधीरपि ॥ 71॥
1.163.m: If leaves too are unavailable, one may offer fruits; / and if fruits are unavailable, even grasses, shrubs, and medicinal plants.

1.163.s:
oṣadhīnāmabhāve tu bhaktyā bhavati pūjitaḥ ..
pratyekaṃ muktapuṣpeṇa daśasauvarṇikaṃ phalam .. 72 ..
1.163.d:
ओषधीनामभावे तु भक्त्या भवति पूजितः ॥
प्रत्येकं मुक्तपुष्पेण दशसौवर्णिकं फलम् ॥ 72 ॥
1.163.m: In the absence of plants, he is worshipped through devotion alone. / For each single dropped flower [offered], the reward equals ten gold coins.

1.163.s:
yaḥ sugandhairmuktapuṣpaiḥ samyagbhānuṃ prapūjayet ..
māghāsite'pi sumanāḥ so'naṃtaphalamaśnute .. 73..
1.163.d:
यः सुगन्धैर्मुक्तपुष्पैः सम्यग्भानुं प्रपूजयेत् ॥
माघासितेऽपि सुमनाः सोऽनंतफलमश्नुते ॥ 73॥
1.163.m: He who properly worships the Sun with fragrant dropped flowers, / being pure of mind, even on the dark [fortnight] of Māgha, obtains endless fruit.

1.163.s:
karavīrairmahārāja saṃyato bhānumarcayet ..
sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ sūryaloke mahīyate .. 74 ..
1.163.d:
करवीरैर्महाराज संयतो भानुमर्चयेत् ॥
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तः सूर्यलोके महीयते ॥ 74 ॥
1.163.m: Restrained, O great king, he should worship the Sun with karavīras; / freed from all sins, he is honoured in the realm of the Sun.

1.163.s:
agastyakusumairbhaktyā yaḥ sakṛdbhānumarcayet..
gavāṃ prayutadānasya phalaṃ prāpya divaṃ vrajet .. 75 ..
1.163.d:
अगस्त्यकुसुमैर्भक्त्या यः सकृद्भानुमर्चयेत्॥
गवां प्रयुतदानस्य फलं प्राप्य दिवं व्रजेत् ॥ 75 ॥
1.163.m: He who with devotion worships the Sun even once with agastya flowers, / having obtained the fruit of giving a million cows, goes to heaven.

1.163.s:
mallikotpalapadmaiśca jātīpunnāgacaṃpakaiḥ ..
aśokaśvetamaṃdārakarṇikārāṃdhukaistathā .. 76 ..
1.163.d:
मल्लिकोत्पलपद्मैश्च जातीपुन्नागचंपकैः ॥
अशोकश्वेतमंदारकर्णिकारांधुकैस्तथा ॥ 76 ॥
1.163.m: With mallikā, blue water-lilies, and lotuses, with jātī, punnāga, and campaka, / with aśoka, white mandāra, karṇikāra, and andhuka,

1.163.s:
karavīrārkakahlāraśamītagarakeśaraiḥ ..
agastibakapuṣpaistu śatapatrairnarādhipa .. 77 ..
1.163.d:
करवीरार्ककह्लारशमीतगरकेशरैः ॥
अगस्तिबकपुष्पैस्तु शतपत्रैर्नराधिप ॥ 77 ॥
1.163.m: with karavīra, arka, kahlāra, śamī, tagara, and keśara, / with flowers of agasti and baka, and with hundred-petalled lotuses, O king—

1.163.s:
puṣpairetairyathālābhaṃ yo naraḥ pūjayedravim ..
sa tatphalamavāpnoti tadekāgramanāḥ śṛṇu .. .. 78 ..
1.163.d:
पुष्पैरेतैर्यथालाभं यो नरः पूजयेद्रविम् ॥
स तत्फलमवाप्नोति तदेकाग्रमनाः शृणु ॥ ॥ 78 ॥
1.163.m: whatever man worships the Sun with these flowers as they are obtained, / he attains that reward; hear of it with single-pointed mind:

1.163.s:
sūryakoṭipratīkāśairvimānaiḥ sarvakāmibhiḥ ..
puṣpamālāparikṣiptairgītavāditranāditaiḥ .. 79 ..
1.163.d:
सूर्यकोटिप्रतीकाशैर्विमानैः सर्वकामिभिः ॥
पुष्पमालापरिक्षिप्तैर्गीतवादित्रनादितैः ॥ 79 ॥
1.163.m: In celestial chariots resembling ten million suns, fulfilling all desires, / wreathed with garlands of flowers, resounding with songs and musical instruments,

1.163.s:
taṃtrīmadhuravādyaiśca svacchaṃdagamanairnṛpa ..
sūryakanyāsamākīrṇairdevānāṃ ca sudurlabhaiḥ .. 1.163.80 ..
1.163.d:
तंत्रीमधुरवाद्यैश्च स्वच्छंदगमनैर्नृप ॥
सूर्यकन्यासमाकीर्णैर्देवानां च सुदुर्लभैः ॥ 1.163.80 ॥
1.163.m: sweet with the playing of stringed instruments, moving at will, O king, / crowded with daughters of the Sun, and exceedingly difficult even for gods to attain,

1.163.s:
dodhūyamānaścamaraiḥ stūyamānaḥ surāsuraiḥ ..
gacchedarkapurīṃ divyāṃ tatra saṃpūjito bhavet .. 81..
1.163.d:
दोधूयमानश्चमरैः स्तूयमानः सुरासुरैः ॥
गच्छेदर्कपुरीं दिव्यां तत्र संपूजितो भवेत् ॥ 81॥
1.163.m: fanned with chowries and praised by gods and asuras, / he would go to the divine city of the Sun, and there he would be honoured.

1.163.s:
yaistaiśca vāpikusumairjalajaiḥ sthalajairnṛpa ..
saṃpūjya śraddhayā bhānumarkaloke mahīyate ..82 ..
1.163.d:
यैस्तैश्च वापिकुसुमैर्जलजैः स्थलजैर्नृप ॥
संपूज्य श्रद्धया भानुमर्कलोके महीयते ॥82 ॥
1.163.m: Having worshipped the Sun with faith, O king, with whatever flowers— / water-born or land-born—he is honoured in the realm of the Sun.

1.163.s:
sūryasyopari yaḥ kuryācchobhanaṃ puṣpamaṃḍalam..
śobhitaṃ puṣpasragdāmairāpīṭhāṃtaṃ pralaṃbitaiḥ .. 83 ..
1.163.d:
सूर्यस्योपरि यः कुर्याच्छोभनं पुष्पमंडलम्॥
शोभितं पुष्पस्रग्दामैरापीठांतं प्रलंबितैः ॥ 83 ॥
1.163.m: He who makes a beautiful floral pavilion above the Sun, / adorned with floral garlands and wreaths hanging down to the pedestal,

1.163.s:
atyāścaryamahāyānairdivyapuṣpopaśobhitaḥ ..
sarveṣāmupariṣṭācca vasedarkapure sukhī .. 84 ..
1.163.d:
अत्याश्चर्यमहायानैर्दिव्यपुष्पोपशोभितः ॥
सर्वेषामुपरिष्टाच्च वसेदर्कपुरे सुखी ॥ 84 ॥
1.163.m: adorned with divine flowers and accompanied by exceedingly wondrous grand vehicles, / dwells happy above all in the city of the Sun.

1.163.s:
anekarāgavinyastaiḥ sugandhaiḥ kusumairgṛham ..
yaḥ kuryātparvakāle tu vicitrakusumojjvalam .. 85 ..
1.163.d:
अनेकरागविन्यस्तैः सुगन्धैः कुसुमैर्गृहम् ॥
यः कुर्यात्पर्वकाले तु विचित्रकुसुमोज्ज्वलम् ॥ 85 ॥
1.163.m: He who on a festival day makes the house radiant with manifold flowers, / with fragrant blossoms arranged in diverse colours,

1.163.s:
sa puṣpakavimānena puṣpamālākulena tu ..
puṣpetarapuraṃ divyaṃ śrayate nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 86 ..
1.163.d:
स पुष्पकविमानेन पुष्पमालाकुलेन तु ॥
पुष्पेतरपुरं दिव्यं श्रयते नात्र संशयः ॥ 86 ॥
1.163.m: he, by means of a floral celestial chariot laden with garlands of flowers, / repairs to the divine city of flowers; of this there is no doubt.

1.163.s:
akṣayaṃ modate kālamatiraskṛtaśāsanaḥ ..
saurādisarvalokeṣu yatreṣṭaṃ tatra yāti saḥ .. 87 .. ..
sūryaṣaṣṭhīvratavarṇanam
1.163.d:
अक्षयं मोदते कालमतिरस्कृतशासनः ॥
सौरादिसर्वलोकेषु यत्रेष्टं तत्र याति सः ॥ 87 ॥ ॥
सूर्यषष्ठीव्रतवर्णनम्
1.163.m:
He rejoices for imperishable time, his command unthwarted; / he goes wherever he desires among all worlds, beginning with the world of Sūrya.
Description of the Sūryaṣaṣṭhī Vrata.

1.164.s:
śatānīka uvāca .. ..
punastvaṃ devadevasya bhāskarasya mahaujasaḥ ..
pūjane yatphalaṃ proktaṃ tanme brūhi dvijottama .. 1
1.164.d:
शतानीक उवाच ॥ ॥
पुनस्त्वं देवदेवस्य भास्करस्य महौजसः ॥
पूजने यत्फलं प्रोक्तं तन्मे ब्रूहि द्विजोत्तम ॥ 1
1.164.m: Śatānīka said: / 'Tell me again, O best of the twice-born, the fruit that is proclaimed / from the worship of Bhāskara, the god of gods, who possesses great splendor.'

1.164.s:
.. sumaṃturuvāca .. ..
śṛṇu tvaṃ hi mahārāja sarvadaṃ lokapūjitam ..
brahmeśopeṃdradevānāṃ trayāṇāmapi bhārata .. 2 ..
1.164.d:
॥ सुमंतुरुवाच ॥ ॥
शृणु त्वं हि महाराज सर्वदं लोकपूजितम् ॥
ब्रह्मेशोपेंद्रदेवानां त्रयाणामपि भारत ॥ 2 ॥
1.164.m: Sumaṃtu said: / 'Listen, O great king, descendant of Bharata, [to what yields] all things and is honored by the world, / even among the three gods Brahmā, Īśa, and Upendra.

1.164.s:
sukhāsīnaṃ surajyeṣṭhaṃ manovatyāṃ caturmukham..
praṇamya śirasā bhūmau viṣṇvīśau vākyamūcatuḥ .. 3 ..
1.164.d:
सुखासीनं सुरज्येष्ठं मनोवत्यां चतुर्मुखम्॥
प्रणम्य शिरसा भूमौ विष्ण्वीशौ वाक्यमूचतुः ॥ 3 ॥
1.164.m: When the four-faced eldest among the gods was seated comfortably in Manovatī, / Viṣṇu and Īśa bowed their heads to the ground and addressed him with these words:

1.164.s:
ya eṣa bhagavāndevaḥ sahasrakiraṇo raviḥ ..
asya yatpūjane puṇyaṃ prāpyate tadvadasva nau .. 4 ..
1.164.d:
य एष भगवान्देवः सहस्रकिरणो रविः ॥
अस्य यत्पूजने पुण्यं प्राप्यते तद्वदस्व नौ ॥ 4 ॥
1.164.m: 'This blessed lord, the thousand-rayed Ravi— / tell us both what merit is obtained from his worship.'

1.164.s:
.. brahmovāca .. ..
sādhu sādhu jagannātha sādhu pṛṣṭo'smi vāmiha ..
tasmācchṛṇutamekāgrau gadato nikhilaṃ mama .. 5 ..
1.164.d:
॥ ब्रह्मोवाच ॥ ॥
साधु साधु जगन्नाथ साधु पृष्टोऽस्मि वामिह ॥
तस्माच्छृणुतमेकाग्रौ गदतो निखिलं मम ॥ 5 ॥
1.164.m: Brahmā said: / 'Splendid, splendid, O Lords of the World! You have asked me well here; / therefore, with one-pointed minds, listen to all that I declare.

1.164.s:
svayamutpādya puṣṇāṇi yaḥ sūryaṃ pūjayetsvayam ..
tāni sākṣātpragṛhṇāti tadbhaktyā satataṃ raviḥ .. 6 ..
1.164.d:
स्वयमुत्पाद्य पुष्णाणि यः सूर्यं पूजयेत्स्वयम् ॥
