अस्मिम्̐ल्लोके चा संप्राप्ता राजानं विंदते पतिम् ॥
चन्द्राग्निभास्कराणां तु कांतितेजःप्रभान्वितम् ॥ 39 ॥
1.168.m:
Having enjoyed pleasures as desired in the world of Sūrya and other realms,
and having arrived in this world, she finds a king as husband,
endowed with the loveliness, splendor, and brilliance of the moon, fire, and sun.

1.168.s:
yaṃyaṃ kāmaṃ samuddiśya naranārīnapuṃsakāḥ ..
pūjayaṃti raviṃ bhaktyā tatsarvaṃ prāpnuvaṃti hi .. 1.168.40 .. ..
sūryavratavarṇanam
1.168.d:
यंयं कामं समुद्दिश्य नरनारीनपुंसकाः ॥
पूजयंति रविं भक्त्या तत्सर्वं प्राप्नुवंति हि ॥ 1.168.40 ॥ ॥
सूर्यव्रतवर्णनम्
1.168.m:
Whatever desire men, women, or eunuchs intend
when they worship Ravi with devotion, all that indeed they obtain.
Description of the Sūryavrata

1.169.s:
.. sumaṃturuvāca .. ..
mṛnmayaṃ dārujaṃ śailaṃ pakveṣṭakamathāpi vā ..
kṛtvā maṭhaṃ gṛhaṃ vāpi yathā vibha vasaṃbhavāt .. 1 ..
1.169.d:
॥ सुमंतुरुवाच ॥ ॥
मृन्मयं दारुजं शैलं पक्वेष्टकमथापि वा ॥
कृत्वा मठं गृहं वापि यथा विभ वसंभवात् ॥ 1 ॥
1.169.m:
Sumantu said:
Having made a monastery or a house of clay, wood, stone,
or baked bricks, according to the extent of one's wealth,

1.169.s:
sarvopakaraṇopetaṃ sarvadhānyasamanvitam ..
sūryāyetthaṃ gṛhaṃ dadyātsarvānkāmānavāpnuyāt .. 2 ..
1.169.d:
सर्वोपकरणोपेतं सर्वधान्यसमन्वितम् ॥
सूर्यायेत्थं गृहं दद्यात्सर्वान्कामानवाप्नुयात् ॥ 2 ॥
1.169.m:
equipped with all utensils, provided with all kinds of grain,
one who gives such a house to Sūrya obtains all desires.

1.169.s:
kṛtvaikabhaktaṃ hemaṃte māghamāsamataṃ dritaḥ ..
māsāṃtena rathaṃ kuryāccitravastropaśobhitam .. 3 ..
1.169.d:
कृत्वैकभक्तं हेमंते माघमासमतं द्रितः ॥
मासांतेन रथं कुर्याच्चित्रवस्त्रोपशोभितम् ॥ 3 ॥
1.169.m:
Having eaten once a day in the cold season throughout the month of Māgha without indolence,
at the end of the month one should make a chariot adorned with variegated cloth,

1.169.s:
śvetaiścaturbhiḥ saṃyuktaṃ turagaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam ..
śvetadhvajapatākābhiśchatracāmaradarpaṇaiḥ .. .. 4 ..
1.169.d:
श्वेतैश्चतुर्भिः संयुक्तं तुरगैः समलंकृतम् ॥
श्वेतध्वजपताकाभिश्छत्रचामरदर्पणैः ॥ ॥ 4 ॥
1.169.m:
yoked to four white horses, richly decorated
with white flags, pennants, royal parasols, chowries, and mirrors.

1.169.s:
taṃḍulāḍhakapiṣṭena kṛtvā bhānuṃ narādhipa ..
vinyasya taṃ rathopasthe saṃjñayā saha bhūpate .. 5 ..
1.169.d:
तंडुलाढकपिष्टेन कृत्वा भानुं नराधिप ॥
विन्यस्य तं रथोपस्थे संज्ञया सह भूपते ॥ 5 ॥
1.169.m:
Having fashioned Bhānu with flour from an āḍhaka of rice, O ruler of men,
and having placed him upon the chariot-seat together with Saṃjñā, O lord of the earth,

1.169.s:
taṃ rātrau rājamārgeṇa śaṃkhabheryādinisvanaiḥ ..
bhramayitvā śanaiḥ paścātsūryāyatanamāviśet .. 6 ..
1.169.d:
तं रात्रौ राजमार्गेण शंखभेर्यादिनिस्वनैः ॥
भ्रमयित्वा शनैः पश्चात्सूर्यायतनमाविशेत् ॥ 6 ॥
1.169.m:
having processed it at night along the royal highway to the sounds of conches, kettledrums, and other instruments,
one should then slowly enter the temple of Sūrya.

1.169.s:
tatra jāgarapūjābhiḥ pradīpāvaliśobhitaiḥ ..
prekṣaṇīyaiḥ pradānaiśca kṣapayitvā śanaiḥ kṣapām ..7 ..
1.169.d:
तत्र जागरपूजाभिः प्रदीपावलिशोभितैः ॥
प्रेक्षणीयैः प्रदानैश्च क्षपयित्वा शनैः क्षपाम् ॥7 ॥
1.169.m:
Having spent the night slowly there with vigils and worships,
shining with rows of lamps, spectacles, and gifts,

1.169.s:
prabhāte snapanaṃ kṛtvā madhukṣīraghṛtena ca ..
dīnāṃdhakṛpaṇebhyo'nnaṃ yathāśaktyā ca dakṣiṇām .. 8 ..
1.169.d:
प्रभाते स्नपनं कृत्वा मधुक्षीरघृतेन च ॥
दीनांधकृपणेभ्योऽन्नं यथाशक्त्या च दक्षिणाम् ॥ 8 ॥
1.169.m:
having performed the bathing at dawn with honey, milk, and clarified butter,
[giving] food to the poor, the blind, and the destitute, and fees according to one's capacity,

1.169.s:
rathaṃ saṃvāhanopetaṃ bhāskarāya nivedayet..
bhuktvā ca bāṃdhavaiḥ sārdhaṃ praṇamyārkagṛhaṃ vrajet ..9..
1.169.d:
रथं संवाहनोपेतं भास्कराय निवेदयेत्॥
भुक्त्वा च बांधवैः सार्धं प्रणम्यार्कगृहं व्रजेत् ॥9॥
1.169.m:
one should dedicate the chariot together with the draft animals to Bhāskara;
and having eaten together with kinsmen, bowing down, one should go to the house of Arka.

1.169.s:
sarvavratānāṃ pravaraṃ maṃtradharmānvitaḥ sadā ..
vrataṃ sūryavrataṃ nāmasarvakāmārthasiddhaye ..1.169.10..
1.169.d:
सर्वव्रतानां प्रवरं मंत्रधर्मान्वितः सदा ॥
व्रतं सूर्यव्रतं नामसर्वकामार्थसिद्धये ॥1.169.10॥
1.169.m:
The observance called Sūryavrata is always the best of all observances,
joined with mantras and righteousness, for the attainment of all desired goals.

1.169.s:
sarvavrateṣu yatpuṇyaṃ sarvayajñeṣu yatphalam ..
sarvaṃ sūryaratheneha tatpuṇyaṃ labhate nṛpa .. 11 ..
1.169.d:
सर्वव्रतेषु यत्पुण्यं सर्वयज्ञेषु यत्फलम् ॥
सर्वं सूर्यरथेनेह तत्पुण्यं लभते नृप ॥ 11 ॥
1.169.m:
Whatever merit is in all observances, whatever fruit is in all sacrifices,
all that merit one obtains here by means of the chariot of Sūrya, O king.

1.169.s:
sūryāyutapratīkāśairvimānaiḥ sārvakāmikaiḥ ..
trisaptakulajaiḥ sārdhaṃ sūryaloke mahīyate .. 12 ..
1.169.d:
सूर्यायुतप्रतीकाशैर्विमानैः सार्वकामिकैः ॥
त्रिसप्तकुलजैः सार्धं सूर्यलोके महीयते ॥ 12 ॥
1.169.m:
On celestial chariots fulfilling all desires, resembling ten thousand suns,
he is glorified in the world of Sūrya together with relatives of twenty-one generations.

1.169.s:
bhuktvā tu vipulānbhogānsarvalokeṣvanukramāt ..
kalpāyutaśataṃ sāgraṃ tato rājā bhavetkṣitau .. 13 ..
1.169.d:
भुक्त्वा तु विपुलान्भोगान्सर्वलोकेष्वनुक्रमात् ॥
कल्पायुतशतं साग्रं ततो राजा भवेत्क्षितौ ॥ 13 ॥
1.169.m:
Having enjoyed abundant pleasures in all worlds in succession
for a full hundred myriad kalpas, he then becomes a king on earth.

1.169.s:
paṃcabalisamāyuktaṃ mṛdu ṣaḍvāstukalpitam ..
sarvopakaraṇopetaṃ sūryaṃ saṃjñāṃ prakalpayet .. 14 ..
1.169.d:
पंचबलिसमायुक्तं मृदु षड्वास्तुकल्पितम् ॥
सर्वोपकरणोपेतं सूर्यं संज्ञां प्रकल्पयेत् ॥ 14 ॥
1.169.m:
Accompanied by five offerings, soft, arranged on six sites,
equipped with all utensils, one should fashion Sūrya and Saṃjñā.

1.169.s:
saṃjñādevīsamāyuktaṃ paiṣṭāśāḍhyaṃ nivedayet..
saurajñānārthatattvajñamācāryamudayānvitam .. 15 ..
1.169.d:
संज्ञादेवीसमायुक्तं पैष्टाशाढ्यं निवेदयेत्॥
सौरज्ञानार्थतत्त्वज्ञमाचार्यमुदयान्वितम् ॥ 15 ॥
1.169.m:
Accompanied by the goddess Saṃjñā, one should offer [a figure] rich with flour of Āṣāḍha [rice];
and to an ācārya who knows the true essence of the Saura knowledge, endowed with prosperity,

1.169.s:
saṃpūjya gaṃdhapuṣpādyairvastrālaṃkāracāmaraiḥ ..
bhakṣya bhojyairaśeṣaiśca tataḥ śayyāṃ nivedayet .. 16 ..
1.169.d:
संपूज्य गंधपुष्पाद्यैर्वस्त्रालंकारचामरैः ॥
भक्ष्य भोज्यैरशेषैश्च ततः शय्यां निवेदयेत् ॥ 16 ॥
1.169.m:
having worshipped [him] with perfumes, flowers, and the like, with garments, ornaments, and chowries,
and with all kinds of solid and soft foods, one should then present a bed.

1.169.s:
tadūrṇātūlavastrāṇāṃ parisaṃkhyā tu yāvatī ..
tāvadvarṣasahasrāṇi sūryaloke mahīyate .. 17 ..
1.169.d:
तदूर्णातूलवस्त्राणां परिसंख्या तु यावती ॥
तावद्वर्षसहस्राणि सूर्यलोके महीयते ॥ 17 ॥
1.169.m:
As great as is the count of threads of its wool, cotton, and garments,
for that many thousands of years he is glorified in the world of Sūrya.

1.169.s:
surādisarvalokeṣu bhuktvā bhogānaśeṣataḥ ..
kāmādāgatya loke'sminrājā bhavati dhārmikaḥ .. 18 ..
1.169.d:
सुरादिसर्वलोकेषु भुक्त्वा भोगानशेषतः ॥
कामादागत्य लोकेऽस्मिन्राजा भवति धार्मिकः ॥ 18 ॥
1.169.m:
Having enjoyed all pleasures in all the worlds of the gods and others,
returning to this world as he desires, he becomes a righteous king.

1.169.s:
daśa gobhiḥ saha vṛṣaṃ tā vṛṣaikādaśāḥ smṛtāḥ ..
sūryāya vinivedyeha yatphalaṃ labhate śṛṇu .. 19 ..
1.169.d:
दश गोभिः सह वृषं ता वृषैकादशाः स्मृताः ॥
सूर्याय विनिवेद्येह यत्फलं लभते शृणु ॥ 19 ॥
1.169.m:
Hear what fruit one obtains here upon dedicating to Sūrya
a bull together with ten cows—these are known as the eleven cattle headed by a bull.

1.169.s:
dvādaśādityatulyātmā aṇimādiguṇairyutaḥ ..
sarvatra modate rājansūryasyānucaro bhavet .. 20 .. ..
godānavarṇanam
1.169.d:
द्वादशादित्यतुल्यात्मा अणिमादिगुणैर्युतः ॥
सर्वत्र मोदते राजन्सूर्यस्यानुचरो भवेत् ॥ 20 ॥ ॥
गोदानवर्णनम्
1.169.m:
Equal in nature to the twelve Ādityas, endowed with virtues such as atomicity,
he rejoices everywhere, O king, and becomes an attendant of Sūrya.
Description of the Gift of Cows

1.170.s:
.. sumanturuvāca .. ..
savṛṣaṃ gośataṃ dattvā bhāskarāya narādhipa ..
triḥsaptakulajaiḥ sārdhaṃ śṛṇu yatphalamāpnuyāt .. 1 ..
1.170.d:
॥ सुमन्तुरुवाच ॥ ॥
सवृषं गोशतं दत्त्वा भास्कराय नराधिप ॥
त्रिःसप्तकुलजैः सार्धं शृणु यत्फलमाप्नुयात् ॥ 1 ॥
1.170.m:
Sumantu said:
Having given a hundred cows together with a bull to Bhāskara, O ruler of men,
hear what fruit one obtains together with relatives of twenty-one generations:

Resembling crores of the finest beings, endowed with all desires,
upon countless great vehicles worshipped by gods and asuras,

1.170.s:
dvādaśādityasaṃkāśo divākara ivāparaḥ ..
gatvādityapuraṃ ramyaṃ krīḍate sūryamaṃḍape .. 3 ..
1.170.d:
द्वादशादित्यसंकाशो दिवाकर इवापरः ॥
गत्वादित्यपुरं रम्यं क्रीडते सूर्यमंडपे ॥ 3 ॥
1.170.m:
resembling the twelve Ādityas, like another Divākara,
having gone to the delightful city of Āditya, he sports in the pavilion of Sūrya.

1.170.s:
bhuktvā tu vipulānbhogānpralaye sarvadehinām ..
mohakaṃcukamutsṛjya viśatyādityamaṃḍale .. 4 ..
1.170.d:
भुक्त्वा तु विपुलान्भोगान्प्रलये सर्वदेहिनाम् ॥
मोहकंचुकमुत्सृज्य विशत्यादित्यमंडले ॥ 4 ॥
1.170.m:
Having enjoyed abundant pleasures, at the dissolution of all embodied beings,
casting off the bodice of delusion, he enters the solar orb.

1.170.s:
sarvajñaḥ sūraparamaḥ śuddhaḥ svātmanyavasthitaḥ ..
sarvagaḥ paripūrṇatvātsūryavaddīptimānbhavet .. 5..
1.170.d:
सर्वज्ञः सूरपरमः शुद्धः स्वात्मन्यवस्थितः ॥
सर्वगः परिपूर्णत्वात्सूर्यवद्दीप्तिमान्भवेत् ॥ 5॥
1.170.m:
All-knowing, devoted to Sūra, pure, established in his own self,
all-pervading through his fullness, he becomes radiant like the sun.

1.170.s:
yo dadyādubhayamukhīṃ saurabheyīṃ divākare ..
saptadvīpāṃ mahīṃ dattvā yatphalaṃ tadavāpnuyāt ..
pādadvayaṃ śiro'rdhaṃ ca saśailavanakānanā .. 6 ..
bhojakabhojanānuṣṭhānavarṇanam
1.170.d:
यो दद्यादुभयमुखीं सौरभेयीं दिवाकरे ॥
सप्तद्वीपां महीं दत्त्वा यत्फलं तदवाप्नुयात् ॥
पादद्वयं शिरोऽर्धं च सशैलवनकानना ॥ 6 ॥
भोजकभोजनानुष्ठानवर्णनम्
1.170.m:
Whoever gives to Divākara a cow with two heads [at calving],
what fruit [one obtains] by giving the earth with its seven continents,
with its mountains, woods, and forests, that he obtains [when only] two feet and half the head [are born].
Description of the rules of dining for Bhojakas
